data.title: Tachy0n: The Last 0day Jailbreak
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Siguza在2020年发现并利用的一个iOS内核漏洞（tachy0n），该漏洞影响了iOS 13.0至13.5，并在unc0ver v5.0.0中发布。这是当时一个罕见的0day漏洞，因为苹果在一周后为此专门发布了补丁。作者解释了这个漏洞的发现过程，以及它如何通过回归测试被重新找到。漏洞存在于lio_listio系统调用中，涉及一个竞态条件，导致内核内存重复释放，从而可以被利用进行内核权限提升。这个漏洞的特殊之处在于它曾被当作1day使用过，但由于苹果的疏忽，它未被完全修复，最终成为0day。作者还回顾了类似漏洞的历史，如SockPuppet，强调了苹果在回归测试方面的不足。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果设备越狱、漏洞修复以及回归测试的有效性

不同观点：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 认为苹果公司在修复漏洞时缺乏有效的回归测试机制，导致已经修复的漏洞重新出现在新版本中。他指出，通过简单的回归测试可以发现这些漏洞，并推测其他开源项目可能也存在类似机会。他还举例说明了iOS 12中SockPuppet漏洞的重复出现，并提出疑问，是否有其他项目在进行类似的历史漏洞回归测试。

• [0x38B] 表示对复杂技术细节的理解困难，提到对越狱技术的怀念，但并没有深入讨论技术问题。他提到自己曾尝试过越狱，但并没有实际用途，只是觉得有趣。他还提到SideStore看起来有前途，但由于其开发者账户问题无法安装某些应用。

• [weinzierl] 提到苹果现在为越狱漏洞支付高额赏金，暗示越狱发现漏洞对苹果来说具有商业价值。

• [Tachyooon] 表示对讨论内容有个人共鸣，但未深入探讨技术细节。

• [greggh] 以幽默的方式表达对漏洞重新出现的态度，赞赏重新引入漏洞的人，带有调侃意味。

• [ivanjermakov] 认为苹果通过锁定设备防止越狱，实际上利用越狱开发者免费发现的漏洞进行自我修复，是一种聪明的策略。

• [Hilift] 对未来五年设备安全性表示担忧，特别提到iMessage仍存在设备和数据接管的风险。

• [peterburkimsher] 关注越狱是需要连接电脑（tethered）还是无需连接（untethered）的方式，显示出对越狱实际使用场景的关注。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及苹果公司漏洞修复流程的缺陷以及回归测试的重要性。
• 越狱技术的娱乐价值与实用性被提及，反映出部分用户对越狱的兴趣。
• 对苹果安全策略的有效性存在不同看法，有人认为其策略聪明有效，有人则对其长期安全性表示担忧。
• 对越狱漏洞的商业价值也有提及，显示出漏洞发现与修复的市场化趋势。

44083388.article_content:
Siguza, 23. May 2025
tachy0n
The last 0day jailbreak.
0. Introduction
Hey.
Long time no see, huh?
People have speculated over the years that someone “bought my silence”, or asked me whether I had moved my blog posts to some other place, but no. Life just got in the way.
This is not the blog post with which I planned to return, but it’s the one for which all the research is said and done, so that’s what you’re getting. I have plenty more that I wanna do, but I’ll be happy if I can even manage to put out two a year.
Now,
tachy0n
. This is an old exploit, for iOS 13.0 through 13.5, released in
unc0ver
v5.0.0 on May 23rd, 2020, exactly 5 years ago today. It was a fairly standard kernel LPE for the time, but one thing that made it noteworthy is that it was dropped as an 0day, affecting the latest iOS version at the time, leading Apple to
release a patch
for just this bug a week later. This is something that used to be common a decade ago, but has become extremely rare - so rare, in fact, that is has never happened again after this.
Another thing that made it noteworthy is that, despite having been an 0day on iOS 13.5, it had actually been exploited before - by me and friends - but as a 1day at the time. And that is where this whole story starts.
In early 2020,
Pwn20wnd
(a jailbreak author, not to be confused with Pwn2Own, the event) contacted me, saying he had found an 0day reachable from the app sandbox, and was asking whether I’d be willing to write an exploit for it. At the time I had been working on
checkra1n
for a couple of months, so I figured going back to kernel research was a welcome change of scenery, and I agreed. But where did this bug come from? It was extremely unlikely that someone would’ve just sent him this bug for free, with no strings attached. And despite being a jailbreak author, he wasn’t doing security research himself, so it was equally unlikely that he would discover such a bug. And yet, he did.
The way he managed to beat a trillion dollar corporation was through the kind of simple but tedious and boring work that Apple sucks at: regression testing.
Because, you see: this has happened before. On iOS 12,
SockPuppet
was one of the big exploits used by jailbreaks. It was found and reported to Apple by
Ned Williamson
from Project Zero, patched by Apple in iOS 12.3, and subsequently unrestricted on the Project Zero bug tracker. But against all odds, it then resurfaced on iOS 12.4, as if it had never been patched. I can only speculate that this was because Apple likely forked XNU to a separate branch for that version and had failed to apply the patch there, but this made it evident that they had no regression tests for this kind of stuff. A gap that was both easy and potentially very rewarding to fill. And indeed, after implementing regression tests for just a few known 1days, Pwn got a hit.
So just for a moment, forget everything you know about kheap separation, forget all the task port mitigations, forget SSV and SPTM… and let’s look at some stuff from the good old times.
1. Lightspeed
First, a quick recap on this bug. This is the
Lightspeed
bug from Synacktiv (CVE-2020-9859 and possibly CVE-2018-4344). It’s in the
lio_listio
syscall, which lets you do asynchronous and/or batched file I/O. To keep track of all submitted I/O ops, the kernel allocates this struct:
struct
aio_lio_context
{
int
io_waiter
;
int
io_issued
;
int
io_completed
;
};
The actual work is then performed on a separate thread, which is also responsible for freeing this struct once all I/O has been completed (in
do_aio_completion
):
/* Are we done with this lio context? */
if
(
lio_context
->
io_issued
==
lio_context
->
io_completed
)
{
lastLioCompleted
=
TRUE
;
}
/*
* free the LIO context if the last lio completed and no thread is
* waiting
*/
if
(
lastLioCompleted
&&
(
waiter
==
0
))
{
free_lio_context
(
lio_context
);
}
But in the case where
nothing
has been scheduled at all, that code path will never be hit, and so the
current
thread has to free this struct again, right from
lio_listio
:
case
LIO_NOWAIT
:
/* If no IOs were issued must free it (rdar://problem/45717887) */
if
(
lio_context
->
io_issued
==
0
)
{
free_context
=
TRUE
;
}
break
;
if
(
free_context
)
{
free_lio_context
(
lio_context
);
}
The problem is just that this check is racy. If work
has
been submitted to the other thread, but it has
already completed
by the time this check runs, then
lio_context
is a dangling pointer here. You can check the
original blog post
for more details, but in order to exploit this, we want the following sequence of events:
lio_listio
allocates
lio_context
.
The work completes and
do_aio_completion
frees
lio_context
.
We reallocate the freed memory with something we control, such that
lio_context->io_issued == 0
.
lio_listio
sees
lio_context->io_issued == 0
and frees our allocated object.
We reallocate it again with something else, and now have two entirely different allocations pointing to the same memory.
Now, we’re targeting 64

data.title: How to Install Windows NT 4 Server on Proxmox
data.author: thepipetogrep
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在Proxmox环境中安装Windows NT 4 Server。由于Windows NT 4在虚拟化环境中表现不佳，作者提供了详细的安装步骤，以尽量减少问题。所需工具包括Proxmox虚拟环境、Windows NT 4 Server的ISO镜像、Realtek 8139网卡驱动、LSI 53C895A SCSI控制器驱动、Windows NT 4 Service Pack 6高加密版本、以及Universal VBE视频显示驱动等。

安装步骤包括：
1. 通过Proxmox的网页界面上传所有ISO文件。
2. 创建新的虚拟机（VM），配置包括使用LSI 53C895A SCSI控制器和Realtek RTL8139网卡。
3. 将SCSI驱动转换为软盘镜像并通过命令行配置。
4. 安装过程中通过F6键加载其他存储驱动。
5. 使用MS Loopback Adapter绕过网卡安装的Bug。
6. 安装Service Pack 6，并修复鼠标不同步问题。
7. 安装Universal VBE视频驱动以支持高色彩和分辨率。

通过这些步骤，用户可以在Proxmox中成功安装和运行Windows NT 4 Server。

• watersb分享了自己撰写关于Windows NT Server 4书籍的经历，并提到当时使用的Banyan Vines网络技术，以及对Active Directory之前的技术背景的介绍。
• simonjgreen怀念NT时代的on-prem（本地部署）优先的心态，并对现代云计算和传统技术之间的优劣进行了反思。

补充讨论：

• LeoPanthera质疑NT 4 Server相对于2000 Server的独特价值，除了在非x86架构（Alpha, MIPS, PowerPC）上的应用。
• ComputerGuru反驳了NT 4虚拟化困难的观点，并提到自己使用VMware Workstation的正面经验。
• jacob019和mr_tox都表达了对复古风格博客的喜爱。
• reconnecting询问了选择NT 4 Server而非Workstation版本的原因，认为后者可能更轻量和易于设置。
• jetbalsa分享了在OpenStack和QEMU环境中安装NT 4的经验，并提到成功运行DOS 6.22的案例。
• Lammy提供了大量关于NT 4磁盘大小限制和技术解决方案的详细信息，并推荐了UniATA驱动。
• WarOnPrivacy分享了在NT 4上启用USB支持的经验，并提供了一个第三方资源的链接。
• racingmars希望Apache Guacamole的RDP客户端能支持NT 4 Terminal Server的旧版RDP协议。

争议焦点：
• NT 4在现代虚拟化环境中的适用性和性能问题，特别是SMP支持和CPU使用率的问题，不同用户提出了不同的解决方案和经验。
• NT 4和Windows 2000之间的优劣比较，特别是在兼容性和功能性方面。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对复古技术（如NT 4和Windows 2000）的怀旧情绪和技术热情。
• 详细的技术文档和经验分享，特别是关于NT 4在现代虚拟化环境中的配置和优化。
• 对现代云计算技术与传统on-prem技术的对比和反思。

44084885.article_content:
How to Install Windows NT 4 Server on Proxmox
Published on: 2025-05-23 18:41:50 • 5 min read
Windows NT 4 Server Boot Screen
What?
Windows NT 4 doesn't virtualise well. This guide shows how to do it with Proxmox with a minimal amount of pain.
Why?
I never got to use it and I only have so much room for old computers.
You Will Need
Proxmox Virtual Environment
Windows NT 4 Server ISO
Realtek 8139 Network Card drivers converted into an ISO file.
My ISO converted copy
Original driver source
LSI 53C895A SCSI controller drivers converted to a floppy image.
My floppy converted copy
Original driver source
Windows NT 4 Service Pack 6 High Encryption version
. WinWorld offers the high encryption version of the installer but the standard encryption version of SP6 so it refuses to install. That is why I grabbed SP6 from archive.org instead.
Universal VBE Video Display Driver converted to an ISO. I used the beta 2015.01.01 version.
My ISO converted copy
Original driver source
VMware tools 3.5.0 ISO
(for the vmmouse driver).
Here is the
Wayback Machine copy
in case the original one goes down.
VM Creation
First upload all the ISO files thorough Proxmox's web interface. Now create a new VM with these settings.
General
ISO Image:
en_winnt_4.0_svr.iso
OS
Guest OS Type:
Microsoft Windows
Guest OS Version:
2000
System
Graphic card:
Standard VGA
. This will allow for higher resolution settings rather than with the default.
SCSI Controller:
LSI 53C895A
Disks
Disk size:
4GB
. I could not get it to format a boot drive larger than this.
Bus/Device:
SCSI
.
IMPORTANT:
Do NOT use IDE. It will be slow noticeably slower and for some reason leads to file system corruption on NT4 guests despite changing the caching options.
CPU
Sockets:
1
Cores:
1
Type:
Pentium
.
IMPORTANT:
The default CPU selection will lead to an immediate BSOD from the installer.
Memory
Memory (MiB):
256
. 32 or higher will suffice.
Network
Model:
Realtek RTL8139
.
This post
says to manually edit the VM config to enable the AMD PCNET card which NT4 has built in support for, but it only runs at 10 Mb/s. The RTL8139 will allow for 100 Mb/s, but we have to install the driver post installation.
Now we have to make the SCSI drivers available to the Windows installer. It only accepts additional mass storage drivers as a floppy disk. Proxmox does not have a web interface for managing floppies so we have to configure this from the command line. Replace
VM_ID
in the following steps with the ID of your VM.
Transfer lsi_533895a_floppy.img to the Proxmox server and move it to
/var/lib/vz/images/VM_ID/floppy.img
.
Open
/etc/pve/qemu-server/VM_ID.conf
, add this to the bottom, then save.
args: -drive file=/var/lib/vz/images/VM_ID/floppy.img,if=floppy,index=0
OS Installation
Switch to the VM's console, start the VM, then begin pressing F6 when you see the Proxmox logo. Keep pressing until you see this screen.
Press the
S
key.
Select
Other
Press
Enter
Press
Enter
again to select
Symbios PCI SCSI High Performance Driver
You should now see
Symbios PCI SCSI High Performance Driver
in the list of mass storage devices. Press
Enter
.
Continue through the installation steps being sure to format the drive as
NTFS
.
When the graphical installer comes up, you will notice the mouse is difficult to use. We will fix that in a later step. Struggle with the mouse or use the keyboard for the rest of the installation.
Continue the installation until you get to the Network Adapter search screen. Click
Select from list...
Select
MS Loopback Adapter
.
IMPORTANT
. Do NOT select "Have Disk" and install the RTL8139 drivers now. It will get stuck on installing TCP/IP and you will have to start over. We're using the MS Loopback Adapter to get around this bug.
Continue through the installer until it asks if there is a DHCP server on your network. Select
No
.
Enter an IP address. Anything will do. We will be replacing it later.
Finish the installation and restart.
Service Pack 6 Installation
Press CTRL-ALT-DEL through the Proxmox console and login as Administrator.
In the VM hardware settings, switch to the ISO containing the Service Pack 6 installer.
Back in the console, navigate to the CD-ROM drive and run the installer.
Reboot.
Go to Start > Run, then run
winver
to verify your results.
Mouse Drivers
Lets fix the wonky mouse.
In the VM hardware settings, switch to the ISO containing VMware Tool 3.5.0.
Back in the console, close the VMware tools installer. Go to
Start > Settings > Control Panel > Mouse
.
In the
General
tab, click
Change...
Click
Have Disk...
Click
Browse...
and navigate to
D:\program files\VMware\VMware Tools\Drivers\mouse\winnt
.
Finish installing the VMware Pointing Device driver then reboot.
Now the mouse in the VM should be perfectly synchronized.
Display Drivers
This is necessary to get high color and resolution support.
In the VM hardware settings, switch to the ISO containing the Universal VBE Video Display Driver.
Back in the console, open
Display Properties
then click
Display Type...
.

data.article_summary:
这篇博客讨论了设计文件格式时需要考虑的几个关键问题和建议：

1. **是否已有合适文件格式**：在设计新格式前，先检查是否已有现成的格式能满足需求，尤其是对于特定用途（如自定义硬件），可能需要自定义格式。

2. **是否需要人类可读**：如果需要人类可读，考虑使用JSON、XML等常见格式，但要注意数据结构。如果不使用这些格式，确保设计易于解析且避免歧义，比如用0和1表示布尔值。

3. **二进制文件分块**：对于不需要人类可读的文件，采用分块的二进制格式更简单。每个块包含标签和长度，可以嵌套，便于扩展和兼容。

4. **允许部分解析**：设计文件格式时，确保可以部分解析，以便不同工具可以读取文件的不同部分。

5. **版本控制**：即使不计划更改格式，也在头部添加版本号字段，以防未来需要，减少后期麻烦。

这些建议旨在帮助设计高效、易用和兼容性好的文件格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文件格式的设计原则，包括可读性、兼容性、容器选择、压缩、索引放置等方面。

不同观点：
• lifthrasiir认为现有文件格式很少遵循理想的设计原则，但这些原则应在处理多种格式时自然形成。他强调了文本数字处理的复杂性，建议在需要处理大量数字时使用二进制格式，并提醒分块（chunking）不一定提供重新排序或前后兼容性。他推荐考虑使用现有格式作为容器，如sBOX或RFC 9277 CBOR-labeled data tags。
• shakna分享了处理未标记分块格式的负面经验，指出XV2保存文件随着版本变化，且缺乏自识别信息，部分内容需要猜测，某些块甚至需要通过网络请求获取更多信息。
• Const-me建议在包含多流的文件格式中使用ZIP作为容器，因为其支持标准工具和多种语言库，并且压缩功能可选择性启用。该格式在多种实际应用中被广泛使用，如MS office文件、Java和Android二进制文件等。
• Dwedit指出，当需要在一个文件中打包多个可增长和删除的文件时，实际上是在要求一个文件内的文件系统，并建议使用文件系统库（如FAT32）来实现。
• InsideOutSanta质疑文件扩展名字符长度的限制，建议使用更长的扩展名以减少碰撞概率，并认为这不会对操作系统兼容性产生问题，只是审美上的不习惯。
• codingjerk赞同分块二进制文件和文档格式的重要性，强调这些措施在受限环境中尤为重要。
• zzo38computer推荐DER格式，因其支持部分解析且易于忽略不需要的部分，并批评了一些现代格式（如JSON）的不足，特别是在Unicode和数据类型方面的限制。
• thasso建议将索引放在文件末尾，以便于追加数据和实现简单的连接操作。
• leiserfg提议在二进制文件中直接使用SQLite。
• mjevans讨论了压缩算法的选择应基于具体用例，权衡速度和压缩效率。
• nikeee指出，对于可能需要版本控制的文件格式，使其可"diffable"是有益的。
• layer8质疑解析器是否会遵循文件头中的字段，指出过去的经验中解析器常常只使用固定的偏移量。
• teddyh引用了Fred Brooks的名言，强调良好的文件和数据格式设计的重要性。
• adelpozo补充建议使文件格式可流式处理或至少允许远程高效读取。
• ahoka警告不要为了节省少量位而设计过于巧妙的格式，如使用一个字节的不同部分存储不同信息。

补充讨论：
• 文件格式的兼容性和可扩展性是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是在版本变更和处理未知块时的挑战。
• 使用现有标准和容器格式被多次提及，作为简化设计和提高兼容性的有效策略。
• 索引放置、压缩和流式处理等具体技术细节也被广泛讨论，显示了在实际应用中这些设计选择的重要性。
• 争议的焦点在于具体实现中的复杂性和实际操作中的可行性，如解析器的可靠性和格式设计的简洁性之间的平衡。

On File Formats
May 19th, 2025
(permalink)
I've been meaning to write something about file format design for a while, and might as well do a blog post. This is pretty unorganized, in a moment thing, so take it as it is.
So You Need a File Format
There's a few questions you have to ask. Different files have different goals, after all.
1. Does a file format exist for this yet?
It's a good idea to check what the prior art is, as it's more than likely that there's already something out there that fits the bill. Let's say you need an image format. There's tons of image formats out there, so one of those might already solve your problem, possibly with tool integration and plenty of library code to boot.
But it's also possible you're in need of a image format for something really specific, like a 4-bit cpu driving a custom LCD with a strange pixel order pattern. Hitting that with jpeg is probably not the way to go. So you need something custom. Assuming, again, that the community for that specific use case doesn't already have a standard format. That you don't have a problem with.
There are cases where you may want to use existing complex systems, such as SQLite, or something that automatically serializes your data; some programming languages even provide functionality for that. There are pros and cons for these approaches, so you may end up having to design something from scratch.
2. Does it need to be human readable?
Parsing text is a pain, so again you need to ask whether you can get away with json, xml, ini or some other commonly used format, and just design fields in it. Just picking one of these formats isn't the end, though, since the structure of the data matters.
There may be a reason you don't want to use those formats, in which case you need to make decisions based on your specific use case, and the reasons why you can't use a common format. In this case I would concentrate on minimizing potential errors, both technical and human; Make the format as easy and foolproof to parse as possible to avoid plenty of headaches ahead (and you may want to avoid
fscanf
for its quirks), and make the human-editable data as unambiguous as possible: if you need true/false values, pick one set and stick to them. I would use 0 and 1 as it's harder to typo "0" than "Disabled".
3. Chunk your binaries.
If the data doesn't need to be human readable, it's often way easier to make a binary format. A common structure for these is a "chunked" format used by various file formats including 3d studio .3ds files, autodesk animator .fli/.flc, EA's .iff (famous on amiga), Apple's .aiff, Microsoft's riff (including .avi) and countless others. The basic idea is to define data in chunks, where each chunk starts with two standard fields: tag and chunk length. Chunks may also contain other chunks, meaning your whole file can be one chunk that then contains other chunks inside it. You can find the whole file size by just checking the root chunk size.
Some people call the initial bytes "magic numbers", used to identify the format. I just call it the tag of the root chunk. Having the whole file be a chunk has the additional benefit of being able to concatenate your files into one bigger file, if need be.
As an example, let's say you have a file format about cats. You might start your file with a "cats" chunk, meaning the first 4 bytes in your file are "cats", followed by 4 bytes describing the whole file length. After that you might have some header fields such as format version, how many cats are described in this file, maybe a field for identifying what software generated the file, etc. After these, you'd have a bunch of other chunks like "toys" for different cat toys (again starting with the tag, followed by that chunk size), "name" for ideas for cat names, "colr" for different cat color schemes, and so on.
Using a chunked format allows chunks to be in different order, and there may be optional chunks, possibly added in later versions, adding backwards and forwards compatibility. Which leads us to:
4. Allow partial parsing.
Whether your data is in text or binary format, design it so that it's possible to write different tools that read your format, that may be interested in different parts of the file. If I wanted a corpus of 8-bit palettes used in .fli animations, I could just write a tool that skips all chunks until it finds the palette chunks and extract just those.
5. Version your formats.
It doesn't matter whether you never, ever, ever plan to change the format, having a version field in your header doesn't cost much but can save you endless headache down the road. The field can be just a zero integer that your parser ignore

data.title: Google shows off Android XR smart glasses with in-lens display
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Google在2025年5月20日的I/O大会上展示了一款轻量级XR智能眼镜，具有深度集成的Gemini系统和可选的内置镜片显示功能，能够提供转向指示等相关信息。这些眼镜配备摄像头、麦克风和扬声器，可连接智能手机使用应用程序。借助Gemini集成，眼镜能够回答有关周围环境的问题、提供导航和实时翻译。Google高管演示了眼镜如何发送信息、安排预约、拍照以及实时翻译对话。Google计划与Warby Parker和Gentle Monster等公司合作，推出时尚的智能眼镜，以吸引消费者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AR智能眼镜的未来应用及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• 对广告入侵的担忧：benrapscallion认为，未来AR眼镜可能会被用于强制播放广告，并对此表示不满，尤其是当这种技术由谷歌和Facebook等以广告为核心的公司推动时，担忧个人隐私和自由受限。

• 技术可行性与设计问题：dvh对AR眼镜的字幕位置和技术实现（如深色背景上的显示能力）提出了质疑，并提到了过去一些技术演示造假的例子（如Magic Leap的鲸鱼演示），表达了对新产品实际效果的怀疑。

• 隐私与“glasshole”效应：wkat4242和dvfjsdhgfv关注AR眼镜的摄像头功能，担心这会加剧隐私问题，尤其是“glasshole”效应（指佩戴者因过度依赖技术而忽视社交礼仪）。

• 对眼镜佩戴者的适应性：dakiol提出，如何为已经戴眼镜的用户设计AR产品是一个挑战，质疑公司是否会忽略这部分市场或推出定制化方案。

• 作为生产力工具的潜力：wongarsu认为，AR眼镜可能被定位为类似Siri的智能助手，通过增强现实技术提供更直观和丰富的输入输出功能，提升用户的生产力。

• 社会影响与安全隐患：Freak_NL指出，AR眼镜可能会导致新的分心问题，尤其是在交通中，使用者可能看起来在注意周围环境，但实际上注意力集中在导航上，增加了安全隐患。

• 对技术垄断和隐私侵犯的深层担忧：cladopa描绘了一个反乌托邦的未来，担心谷歌等公司通过AR眼镜和实时城市建模获取过多权力，不仅侵犯隐私，还可能为三字机构（如政府情报机构）服务，呼吁警惕这种集中化的权力。

补充讨论：
• 对谷歌眼镜失败后再次尝试的质疑：dvfjsdhgfv对谷歌在Google Glass失败后重新推出AR眼镜表示不解，质疑管理层的决策依据。

• 对技术造假的警惕：dvh提到了过去一些技术演示造假的例子，提醒人们在面对新的技术产品时保持警惕，不要轻信厂商宣传。

争议焦点：
• AR眼镜带来的隐私侵犯与技术滥用问题：部分评论者担心AR眼镜会加剧隐私侵犯问题，并赋予科技公司和政府过多权力，而另一部分评论者则关注其技术实现和市场前景。

Google Shows Off Android XR Smart Glasses With In-Lens Display
Tuesday May 20, 2025 3:12 pm PDT
by
Juli Clover
Google
today showed off
a set of lightweight smart glasses that have deep Gemini integration and an optional in-lens display that can offer up relevant information like turn-by-turn directions.
Made to rival the Meta Ray-Bans and smart glasses coming from Apple in the future, Google's XR glasses feature a camera, microphones, and speakers. They connect to a smartphone for app access, and with Gemini integration, the glasses can answer questions about the wearer's surroundings, provide directions, and offer up live translations.
Gemini is able to use the cameras in the glasses to see what's around the wearer to provide feedback, and Google says the glasses will "see and hear what you do" so they'll understand context and "help you throughout your day." On stage at Google I/O, Google executives demonstrated how the Android XR glasses will be able to send messages to friends, make appointments, snap photos, and translate conversations in real-time.
Google plans to work with companies like Warby Parker and Gentle Monster to create stylish smart glasses that consumers will want to wear.

• 作为生产力工具的潜力：wongarsu认为，AR眼镜可能被定位为类似Siri的智能助手，通过增强现实技术提供更直观和丰富的输入输出功能，提升用户的生产力。

• 社会影响与安全隐患：Freak_NL指出，AR眼镜可能会导致新的分心问题，尤其是在交通中，使用者可能看起来在注意周围环境，但实际上注意力集中在导航上，增加了安全隐患。

• 对技术垄断和隐私侵犯的深层担忧：cladopa描绘了一个反乌托邦的未来，担心谷歌等公司通过AR眼镜和实时城市建模获取过多权力，不仅侵犯隐私，还可能为三字机构（如政府情报机构）服务，呼吁警惕这种集中化的权力。

补充讨论：
• 对谷歌眼镜失败后再次尝试的质疑：dvfjsdhgfv对谷歌在Google Glass失败后重新推出AR眼镜表示不解，质疑管理层的决策依据。

• 对技术造假的警惕：dvh提到了过去一些技术演示造假的例子，提醒人们在面对新的技术产品时保持警惕，不要轻信厂商宣传。

争议焦点：
• AR眼镜带来的隐私侵犯与技术滥用问题：部分评论者担心AR眼镜会加剧隐私侵犯问题，并赋予科技公司和政府过多权力，而另一部分评论者则关注其技术实现和市场前景。

data.title: Infinite Tool Use
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）通过工具调用来完成任务的优势，强调模型应专注于工具调用及其参数，而非直接生成内容。工具承载具体任务和目标，使模型能够将大部分智能外化至更高效、领域特定的程序。文章通过文本编辑、3D生成等例子说明，使用工具允许模型进行多层次生成、灵活编辑和选择性遗忘，避免生成过程中出错和混乱。相比之下，LLM仅靠前向生成难以处理复杂任务，容易出错且难以管理长文本。通过工具使用，模型能不断优化输出，实现更精确和复杂的结果。这种方法有助于解决长上下文管理和生成质量问题，为AI开发提供了新的思路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在工具调用与直接输出方面的优势和应用场景

不同观点：
• PeterStuer认为，扩散LLM在理论上具有不局限于早期生成模型的潜在优势，但实际是否能超越当前带有启发式的标准LLM还有待观察。
• anko提出，人类在进行计算时通常依赖工具（如计算器或代码），而LLM被要求执行类似的任务。他建议，如果只需基本语言能力和工具使用，较小的模型可能就足够，并提到人类短时记忆的局限性可能为模型设计提供借鉴。
• blixt强调，每次与LLM的交互都会增加延迟，并指出当前模型在上下文重用方面的不足。他预测LLM将向模糊虚拟机方向发展，通过输出类似指令的token来实现多条件分支和子程序调用。
• dazzaji反对LLM仅输出工具调用的观点，认为LLM本身具有的价值（如写作、总结、创意 brainstorming）不应被忽视，工具调用只是LLM众多功能中的一部分。
• rahimnathwani对如何将工具调用应用于小说写作感到好奇，并提到一个开源工具Storycraftr，尽管该工具仍需用户协调，且LLM输出整章而非精细编辑。
• ayolisup建议通过创建大纲，然后随机采样部分内容并结合上下文进行修订的循环过程来写作，理想情况下结合人类写作。
• yencabulator提到扩散模型可能以不同方式解决当前问题，但未详细展开。
• ksilobman质疑是否需要为LLM赋予文本编辑器权限以进行小说写作，认为应有更优方案。
• brador则持极端观点，认为人类干预会妨碍更高效和更有创意的生产系统，主张仅赋予目标，其余交由系统自动完成。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的工具调用延迟、模型大小与功能、LLM与工具的结合方式以及具体应用（如小说写作）等问题反映了参与者对LLM未来发展方向的不同见解。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM是否应仅限于工具调用，以及如何在实际应用（如写作和创意任务）中最好地利用LLM的能力。

44086094.article_content:
An LLM should never output anything but tool calls and their arguments.
The tools hold the specific, instantiated state of what the model is doing and its goals, while the model itself holds only the information it requires for its immediate task and some additional context, leading to specialization between the LLM and its tools.
Exclusively working through tools allows models to externalize large parts of their intelligence to more efficient, domain-specific programs.
Table of contents:
Examples
Text Editing
3D Generation
Video Understanding
AI safety
Thoughs on Training
Thoughts on Architecture
Conclusion
Examples
The benefits of infinite tool use are best understood via examples.
Text Editing
Here’s how I wrote this article
so far
: I had an idea and wrote it down in a few bullet points. Then, I wrote the introduction. While doing that, I jumped to the end of the article, added a few more bullet points, and edited others. I started writing this section, interrupted it by writing down an idea about the architecture of such models, then came back here; realized that I should re-write this section, started doing that, edited the introduction to fit, went back to the re-write, and here we are. I’m not even half-way done with the article and I’m sure I already forgot several steps that I took.
Now contrast that with the way an LLM currently writes: It generates text forward-only. (Almost) no matter how good it is, it will make mistakes, especially in out-of-distribution (OOD) domains.
Forward-only generation makes
multi-resolution generation
much more difficult: I as a human can create hundreds of versions of the same article; edit a sentence here and there, write down an idea as a bulletpoint, delete something dumb, turn a bulletpoint into a full section, etc.; in other words, I can interleave actions at different levels of specificity. Imagine how confusing it would be to hold all those edits in memory at once!
Editing through external tools allows for explicit, selective forgetting. LLMs on the other hand either need to generate from most general to most specific in order—a very limiting way of multi-scale generation compared to tool-use—or generate a confusing mess of edits and re-edits and deletions that aren’t true deletions; or re-generate the entire output for every single edit; or just generate the final version all at once.
And while we can train an LLM to backtrack and correct mistakes in the form of
reasoning RL
, the mistakes themselves are baked into its output, and thus into both its own context window and the user answer. The latter is a problem because it makes it hard to produce long, correct outputs, the former because it is confusing to the model itself, at least if the output gets very long.
Additionally, the Chain of Thought (CoT) of reasoners doesn’t address the problem of mistakes in the final answer, even if the CoT contains all the information necessary to produce a great final output, simply because no model is ideal, and sampling errors still happen. Of course, we can interleave CoT and user-output; but then we still commit to part of the final output early.
To be clear, reasoner RL is a great thing which is highly compatible with and even required for infinite tool use and will go a long way on its own, and the failings described above are minor ones, but I nevertheless believe that infinite tool use can improve the framework significantly. In a sense, it’s the logical conclusion of what a lot of companies are currently working towards.
More generally,
extremely long contexts
are difficult to manage for LLMs, but might be required for very complex tasks.
Methods like
Entropix
try to work around these issues by dynamically adapting token-sampling parameters like temperature, by branching and merging on demand, and even backtracking, all based on an external measurement of the model’s entropy. Good sampling strategies will be valuable no matter what, but leaving the editing decisions to the model itself is likely a more scalable approach, as demonstrated to a degree by current reasoners.
The final (and correct) step of this evolution is to simply allow the model to continually improve the final answer
before
dumping it on the user. Give it access to a
full text-editor
that is controllable through special text-commands, and see many benefits:
Multi-abstraction-scale text generation
Effortlessly interleaving those abstraction levels
Backtracking via editing
And the potential issue of going off-course is solved by simply refreshing the model’s memory about fine-grained details (specific sections, sentences, words, what the goal of the whole process is, …) through tool-use.
To be clear, this wouldn’t prevent the model from generating easy answers in forward-only mode. If the LLM wants to directly answer a user without going through an editing process, they can do the equivalent of typing out a quick response and immediately clicking “send” within the tool.

data.title: Wrench Attacks: Physical attacks targeting cryptocurrency users (2024) [pdf]
data.author: pulisse
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加密货币持有者遭遇绑架等犯罪事件的增加及其原因和应对措施

不同观点：
• Adrig: 最近法国发生了两起加密货币相关绑架事件，表明这种情况会变得更糟且更难防范。大多数事件是由“业余”犯罪者实施的，这使得这些事件更加不可预测。
• _tom_: 分享了一篇关于纽约地区加密货币投资者遭遇事件的链接，显示此类事件在其他地方也在发生。
• thasso: 质疑为何拥有传统（非加密）资产的富人较少遭遇此类事件，是否因为他们更低调或有银行等保护措施。
• TheAmazingRace: 强调加密货币持有者应保持低调，不要透露自己的财富，因为伪匿名性和个人密钥的脆弱性使得持有者容易成为目标。持有者应避免讨论自己的资产，因为人性脆弱，容易受到暴力威胁。
• lo0dot0: 认为将这类事件称为“新颖”是自负的，因为人类互相抢夺财物已有数世纪历史。
• imaginator: 提供了Jameson Lopp维护的物理比特币攻击列表链接，并开玩笑说由于通货膨胀，XKCD的5美元扳手攻击已不再可能。
• akrymski: 质疑银行是否仍有其价值。
• jonfromsf: 建议投资于持有比特币的ETF，在传统经纪账户中进行交易，这是最直接和安全的方式。
• anigbrowl: 认为这种情况不需要学术论文来解释，富人如果缺乏良好的个人安全措施且炫耀自己的加密货币财富，自然会成为犯罪分子的目标。
• pluto_modadic: 希望讨论能与YubiKeys攻击或记者在边境被拘留等事件有相似之处。
• specialist: 质疑 stealing crypto 的可行性，并讨论了混币器在隐藏资产链方面的有效性，指出即使在俄罗斯、朝鲜或金三角等地区，最终还是会有实际的冲突。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对加密货币持有者为何容易成为目标的原因分析，包括其财富的公开性和伪匿名性。
• 提出了应对措施，如保持低调、投资传统金融产品等。
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效保护加密货币持有者的安全以及加密货币的伪匿名性是否足够安全。
• 对 stealing crypto 的可行性和技术细节进行了探讨，特别是混币器和区块链技术的实际应用。

通过这些观点，可以看到讨论的核心在于加密货币持有者面临的安全威胁及其应对策略，涉及到技术、社会工程学和个人行为等多方面因素。

data.title: Show HN: Photoshop Clone Built in React
data.author: chase-manning
data.article_summary: React Photo Studio是一款由Chase Manning独立开发的免费在线照片编辑应用，目前处于Beta阶段，许多功能仍在开发中。该项目与任何其他照片编辑产品、品牌或公司无关，完全独立。它基于React技术构建，代码托管在GitHub上，使用MIT许可证。用户可以通过贡献指南参与项目贡献。主要功能包括图像编辑和设计，适合摄影和设计领域使用。网站链接为reactphotostudio.app/。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对多个在线图像编辑工具的功能、完成度以及开源性的评价和期望

不同观点：
• **Brajeshwar**：推荐了两个图像编辑工具。一个是非开源的Photopea，另一个是开源的XP Paint。他提供了XP Paint的源码链接，并对开源项目表示支持。

• **vrighter**：对XP Paint的当前状态表示不满，认为一个工具在被称为“已建成”之前，应该大部分功能是可用的。而XP Paint的多数功能尚未实现或无法正常工作。

• **renerick**：部分同意vrighter的观点，认为XP Paint目前仅实现了静态视觉 reproduction，除了画笔功能外，其他如菜单、按钮、下拉菜单和布局管理等功能都不完善，期望能看到更功能性的演示。

• **maximge**：注意到XP Paint中很多功能标注为“正在开发中”，并对“克隆功能正在开发中”表示关注，暗示对目前可用的功能不满意。

• **janmo**：表示失望，因为几乎每个点击的功能都显示正在开发中，认为这影响了用户体验。

补充讨论：
• **mdhb**：提到实际的Photoshop是使用web组件构建的，暗示对当前XP Paint完成度和功能的进一步期望，可能隐含了对技术实现方式的评论。

争议焦点：XP Paint的当前完成度及其是否能被称为“已建成”工具。用户普遍对其大量功能尚未实现表示失望，并对演示的有限功能感到不满。

44086140.article_summary: React Photo Studio是一款由Chase Manning独立开发的免费在线照片编辑应用，目前处于Beta阶段，许多功能仍在开发中。该项目与任何其他照片编辑产品、品牌或公司无关，完全独立。它基于React技术构建，代码托管在GitHub上，使用MIT许可证。用户可以通过贡献指南参与项目贡献。主要功能包括图像编辑和设计，适合摄影和设计领域使用。网站链接为reactphotostudio.app/。
44086140.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对多个在线图像编辑工具的功能、完成度以及开源性的评价和期望

不同观点：
• **Brajeshwar**：推荐了两个图像编辑工具。一个是非开源的Photopea，另一个是开源的XP Paint。他提供了XP Paint的源码链接，并对开源项目表示支持。

• **vrighter**：对XP Paint的当前状态表示不满，认为一个工具在被称为“已建成”之前，应该大部分功能是可用的。而XP Paint的多数功能尚未实现或无法正常工作。

• **renerick**：部分同意vrighter的观点，认为XP Paint目前仅实现了静态视觉 reproduction，除了画笔功能外，其他如菜单、按钮、下拉菜单和布局管理等功能都不完善，期望能看到更功能性的演示。

• **maximge**：注意到XP Paint中很多功能标注为“正在开发中”，并对“克隆功能正在开发中”表示关注，暗示对目前可用的功能不满意。

• **janmo**：表示失望，因为几乎每个点击的功能都显示正在开发中，认为这影响了用户体验。

补充讨论：
• **mdhb**：提到实际的Photoshop是使用web组件构建的，暗示对当前XP Paint完成度和功能的进一步期望，可能隐含了对技术实现方式的评论。

争议焦点：XP Paint的当前完成度及其是否能被称为“已建成”工具。用户普遍对其大量功能尚未实现表示失望，并对演示的有限功能感到不满。

data.author: sychu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款名为“Wall Go”的游戏的评价与建议

不同观点：
• [正面评价]
  ◦ [pjmlp]: 认为游戏看起来很酷且具有成瘾性，表示祝贺。
  ◦ [joeyrideout]: 对游戏表示赞赏，认为其灵感来源于《The Devil's Plan》，并提出希望能有更多类似游戏，甚至设想线下体验或多人视频游戏版本。
  ◦ [spicybright]: 虽然起初对游戏不熟悉，但最终认为游戏设计巧妙，类似于围棋，对游戏实现和节目创作者表示肯定。

• [对AI的建议]
  ◦ [jfindley]: 提到无法选择“困难”AI，希望有更强的AI，但理解其实现难度。
  ◦ [Mizza]: 认为当前AI挑战性不足，分享了自己的策略并对比AI的策略，指出自己得分更高，但认为该策略在面对更强AI时可能无效。

补充讨论：
• [对游戏规则的疑问]
  ◦ [snarf21]: 对墙壁按玩家颜色区分的规则表示疑惑，最初以为可以穿过自己的墙壁而不能穿过对手的。

争议焦点：
• 当前AI的难度和挑战性是讨论的主要争议点，部分玩家认为AI不够强，不足以提供足够的游戏挑战。

data.title: 'Strange metals' point to a whole new way to understand electricity
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章中关于准粒子模型、电子行为以及电阻与超导性关系的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• elcritch认为文章对研究人员超越准粒子模型的描述很有趣，并将研究人员的进展比喻为挣脱束缚的大象。他赞赏新的实验方法，如“聆听”电子扰动，并指出理论家需要实验数据来避免陷入死胡同。
• dinfinity指出量子场论早已将粒子视为场的激发状态，并对文章未提及这一点表示惊讶。
• bawana关注电子自旋及其在超导性和电阻变化中的作用，提出外部磁场是否会影响超导转变温度或电阻率斜率的问题。
• nonelog引用Qimiao Si的话，强调奇怪金属中新物理现象的存在，认为这是显而易见的。
• kens对文章中电阻率曲线形状的描述感到困惑，询问是二次曲线还是指数曲线。
• sfink将超导性比作电子流动，并用液体流动作比喻，探讨电阻与电子速度之间的关系，但未得出明确结论。
• est用牛顿摆作比喻，试图理解准粒子的概念，表示对文章内容的不确定性。
• baerrie对材料研究中测量纠缠的实际应用感到兴奋，并好奇其他具有线性温度变化的材料。
• countWSS将电子行为比作波粒二象性的光子，并根据文章推测在奇怪金属中电子的粒子属性是否消失，只剩下“电子场”梯度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是文章对电阻率曲线的描述不一致，kens指出了这一点。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是量子场论中粒子描述的视角差异，dinfinity对此提出了批评。
• 自旋在电子行为中的作用以及外部磁场的影响是bawana提出的重要问题，值得进一步探讨。
• 不同评论者对文章中提到的准粒子模型和电子行为的比喻和理解方式各不相同，显示出对复杂物理概念的多样解读。

data.title: Design Pressure: The Invisible Hand That Shapes Your Code
data.author: NeutralForest
data.article_summary: 本文总结了一次名为“设计压力：塑造代码的无形之手”的演讲，讨论了为何即使遵循最佳实践，软件架构仍可能变得怪异。作者分享了相关材料和文章，如不同类型的耦合、吸引人的设计陷阱、通过类型设计使非法状态不可表示等。此外，还推荐了一些视频和书籍，如《Tidy First?》、《Architecture Patterns With Python》和《Domain-Driven Design》等，以帮助深入理解软件设计。文章还提及了一些关于类行为、ORM和异步编程的思考，并提供了进一步学习的资源和个人联系方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件设计、领域模型与数据库设计之间权衡的讨论，以及对具体设计实践的不同看法。

不同观点：
• loevborg：认为在项目初期采用“面向数据库的设计”是合理的，因为初期对领域理解有限，直接引入领域模型可能导致过度设计。随着对领域的理解加深，再逐步引入领域模型和显式映射。这种方法强调在项目的不同阶段进行重构，而不是一开始就追求过多的抽象。

• knallfrosch：分享了在一个全新项目中面临的问题，即在没有现有数据和API的情况下，仍然需要为未来可能的变化做准备。这表明即使在绿地项目中，考虑未来的需求和系统的演化也是必要的。

• g958198：强调设计压力是驱动代码架构最重要的因素，且这种感知是基于直觉的，无法轻易传授或量化。设计决策应考虑系统的长期演化和外部压力，而非仅仅依赖“最佳实践”。

• da39a3ee：对一些具体的技术选择（如attr.ib和attr.s）持批评态度，并认为领域驱动设计（DDD）有时像是一种空洞的潮流。

补充讨论：
• HappMacDonald：提到希望将演讲内容转换为文章形式，因为视频中的口语化内容和旁白在书面阅读时显得不合适。

• vinipolicena：提到演讲内容让他想起了Amundsen's Maxim网站上的观点，暗示可能有相似的设计理念。

• leecommamichael：认为现代开发工具和实践可能鼓励了某种程度的耦合，导致一些开发者缺乏对更广泛架构的理解。

• Noumenon72：提到有人暗示演讲中含有对SQLModel的批评，但自己并未在幻灯片中找到相关内容，且该评论后来被删除，显得有些奇怪。

争议焦点：
• 关于何时以及是否应该在项目初期引入领域模型存在不同看法。loevborg认为初期应避免过度抽象，而knallfrosch则强调即使在绿地项目中也应为未来做准备。
• 对具体技术选择和设计理念（如DDD和某些Python库）的批评和认同，显示出在技术社区中对“最佳实践”的不同理解和接受程度。

44087844.article_content:
Ever had this weird gut feeling that something is off in your code, but couldn’t put the finger on why? Are you starting your projects with the best intentions, following all best practices, and still feel like your architecture turns weird eventually?
So far, I’ve held it at
PyCon US 2025
in Pittsburgh, USA.
Slides on SpeakerDeck
.
Design Pressure: The Invisible Hand That Shapes Your Code
(Sorry for the literal throat-cleaning in the video – I lost my voice the night
before and worked on fumes and Fisherman’s Friends.)
Additional material
Some of the material was referred to directly in the talk but landed on the cutting floor due to time constraints.
They all are highly recommended reading/watching for the topic of software design writ large, though.
Articles
Types of Coupling
by Ben Orenstein
Attractive nuisances in software design
by Paul Ganssle
Designing with types: Making illegal states unrepresentable
by Scott Wlaschin
The Vietnam of Computer Science
by Ted Neward (spoiler: it’s ORMs)
A summary by Jeff Atwood (Coding Horror)
Approximating Sum Types in Python with Pydantic
by William Woodruﬀ
How I Build
by Adam Montgomery
DTOs & Mapping: The Good, the Bad, and the Excessive
by Derek Comartin
An example of a conscious decision process on when to map data and reinforcing my point that it’s a trade-off.
The Typestate Pattern in Rust
by Cliff L. Biffle
This is about Rust, but the concept applies the same to any other language.
What Color is Your Function?
This article argues against async primitives in languages because it causes you to have two different types of functions that behave differently. I don’t fully agree, but I find it interesting to apply this logic to classes.
Arguably, ORM classes and, to a much lesser degree, Pydantic classes, behave very differently than regular classes. Especially, because setting attributes implies I/O which complicates reasoning.
In other words, you have to be aware what kind (color!) of class you’re dealing with when reading code.
Videos
Integrated Tests Are A Scam
by J.B. Rainsberger
The Deep Synergy Between Testability and Good Design
by Michael Feathers
SOLID Principles? Nope, just Coupling and Cohesion
by Derek Comartin
The Rising Sea
by Matthew Drury
Advent of Code
Łukasz Langa’s Keynote PyCon US 2022
Simple Made Easy
by Rich Hickey
Watch it before you call anything “simple” ever again.
Building Protocol Libraries The Right Way
by Cory Benfield
Introducing
Sans I/O
, which is a very related topic about writing I/O-agnostic network protocol libraries.
Functional Core Imperative Shell
by Gary Bernhardt
What Gary calls
Core
, is business logic.
Domain Modeling Made Functional
by Scott Wlaschin
Also available as a
book
.
Books
Tidy First?
by Kent Beck
Very short and very good.
Architecture Patterns With Python
by Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
I will recommend this book in every talk until I die.
Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software
by Eric Evans
This is a thicc, dense book that brings the whole domain modeling topic to its logical conclusion. It’s a great read for advanced developers, the DDD community feels sometimes a tad cultish, though.

data.title: Death of Michael Ledeen, maker of the phony case for the invasion of Iraq
data.author: nabla9
data.article_summary: 迈克尔·莱丁（Michael Ledeen）是美国有争议的国安记者和学者，于2025年5月17日去世，享年83岁。他曾在2003年伊拉克战争前扮演关键角色，参与伪造情报以支持入侵行动。莱丁与意大利军事情报部门合作，伪造了一封声称萨达姆从尼日尔购买铀的信件，该情报随后被布什总统用于其2003年国情咨文。莱丁还参与过1980年抹黑卡特总统弟弟比利·卡特的行动，并推广苏联指使刺杀教皇的错误理论。他在伊拉克战争中的角色是秘密情报操纵的典型案例，导致灾难性后果，包括大量伤亡和伊拉克陷入混乱。莱丁的行动展示了为政治目的而进行的情报操纵及其严重影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于美国入侵伊拉克的背景、影响及相关宣传的讨论

不同观点：
• fillmore认为《The Achilles Trap》一书非常值得推荐，尤其是对那些对美国入侵伊拉克背景感兴趣的人。他强调该书基于详尽的研究，并引用了萨达姆政权内部新近公开的资料，提供了有价值的信息。

• jaybrendansmith表达了对当时宣传和情报操纵的强烈不满，认为2024年选举期间也出现了类似的现象。他指出，自己和朋友当时清楚地意识到情报是捏造的，但真相未能传播，许多人被集体思维所蒙蔽，感到声音被压制。

• stormfather对入侵伊拉克的真正原因表示不解，认为并不是官方声称的理由，也否认了与石油相关的动机，但未提出具体替代原因。

• melling从经济角度批评了伊拉克战争的代价，认为如果投入$2万亿用于医疗研究（如治愈癌症），可能对社会有更大益处。他质疑战争的必要性，并暗示即使面对困难，将资源用于其他领域可能带来更大收益。

• hackandthink对作者Jeff Stein持怀疑态度，调侃其名字像是假名，暗示对信息来源的不信任。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是当时美国政府和媒体对伊拉克战争情报的操纵和宣传，部分评论者（如jaybrendansmith）对此表示强烈反对，认为公众被误导。
• 另一个讨论点是战争的代价和资源分配问题，melling特别指出将巨额资金用于战争不如用于医疗研究更具社会价值。
• 对真实入侵原因的质疑（stormfather）反映了部分人对官方叙述的不信任，但未提供具体替代解释。
• 对信息来源的怀疑（hackandthink）显示了对作者和信息可信度的关注。

Death of a Master Manipulator
Michael Ledeen played a key role in making the phony case for the invasion of Iraq—and other damaging skullduggery.

Michael Ledeen (2018, Formiche.net)
Michael Ledeen, the controversial national security journalist, scholar and schemer who
died
at age 83 on May 17 from complications following a stroke, played a significant covert role leading up to the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq, as well as other productions of false intelligence for political ends.
Ledeen was featured prominently in
The Italian Letter
, a 2007 book by SpyTalk Contributing Editor Peter Eisner and Knut Royce, a Pulitzer Prize-winning  investigative reporter at Newsday. Obituaries published this week gave scant attention to the key role Ledeen played in fabricating intelligence to justify the eventually disastrous military campaign to oust Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein from power. The main goal of toppling the regime was achieved but the succeeding occupation, at a cost of an
estimated $2 trillion
, has been judged a military and diplomatic disaster resulting in 37,000 U.S. casualties, at least 200,000 and possibly a million Iraqi civilians dead due to war-related action, and the creation of a virtual Iranian client state in Baghdad.
It was hardly Ledeen’s first foray into skullduggery. In 1980, according to an investigation five years later by the Wall Street Journal, he was involved in a “
disinformation campaign
” to discredit President Jimmy Carter’s brother Billy to the benefit of Republican candidate Ronald Reagan. He also published discredited theories that Soviet Bulgaria was behind the assassination attempt on Pope John Paul II.  "With
Ronald Reagan
newly installed in the White House,” journalist Craig Unger wrote in
Vanity Fair,
“the so-called Bulgarian Connection made perfect
Cold War
propaganda. Michael Ledeen was one of its most vocal proponents, promoting it on TV and in newspapers all over the world."
Ledeen’s role in the Iraq tragedy is a case study of the manipulation of secret—and blatantly dishonest—intelligence relationships for political aims.
The Italian Letter
found that Ledeen, a behind-the-scenes, unofficial envoy of the George W. Bush administration, was deeply involved with Italian military intelligence, which in turn created a forged letter falsely claiming that Hussein had purchased yellow cake—lightly processed uranium—from Niger to build nuclear weapons. President Bush then used that forged information to declare, in his
2003 State of the Union message
, that, “The British Government has learned that Saddam Hussein recently sought significant quantities of uranium from Africa.”
This is a largely hidden but important chapter in the secret history of America that deserves more attention before time further clouds the facts. A lightly edited excerpt from
The Italian Letter
follows here:
In October 2002, Carlo Rossella, editor of the influential Italian news magazine Panorama, brought aboard Michael Arthur Ledeen, a prominent, controversial American neoconservative, as a columnist. Ledeen, who had longtime CIA contacts, had been allegedly involved in Italian intelligence operations for decades.
Panorama published a question and answer interview with Ledeen in the October 3, 2002 edition of the magazine. The occasion was the publication of Ledeen’s book, “The War Against the Terror Masters.” In the interview … Ledeen echoed administration pablum about Iraq and the ‘Axis of Evil,’ first declared by Bush in his January 29, 2002 State of the Union address. Ledeen said that US intervention was necessary in Iraq but only as part of a “war of liberation” to “free the Iranian, Iraqi, Syrian and Saudi populations from the tyrants” that rule them.
Subscribe
Ledeen advocated US intervention in Iraq and elsewhere. He said: “This intervention is necessary. But  my opinion is that it would be more effective to start with Iran, because that is the easiest country to liberate. There would be not even a need for military intervention: our best weapon is the Iranians themselves, who hate the regime and who are prepared to face great risks to overthrow their tyrants.”
Panorama published at least eighteen commentaries by Ledeen in 2002 and 2003 after that. His columns also appeared regularly in the conservative National Review in the United States.
Ledeen also was a fellow at the neoconservative American Enterprise Institute, where he was an associate of James Woolsey, the former CIA director, as well as of other high-octane defense and intelligence veterans who supported and encouraged the Bush administration’s drive in Iraq. data.title: Writing a Self-Mutating x86_64 C Program (2013)
data.author: kepler471
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了自我修改程序的概念，这种程序在运行时会改变自己的代码。虽然这种做法不常见，且因调试困难、硬件依赖性和代码复杂性而不被推荐，但它具有学术研究价值。文章详细介绍了如何在Linux系统中通过改变内存页权限，使得程序的代码段在运行时可写，从而实现自我修改。具体步骤包括使用`mprotect()`函数更改内存页权限，并通过反汇编工具查看和修改函数的机器码。文章以一个简单的C程序为例，展示了如何通过修改汇编指令来改变程序的行为。需要注意的是，这种技术主要用于学术探索，实际应用中可能被恶意软件利用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自修改代码（self-modifying code）的技术、应用及其挑战

不同观点：
• [积极体验] @ivanjermakov 分享了在SIC-1游戏中编写自修改程序的积极体验，强调了其作为单指令编程游戏的独特性。
• [资源分享] @Cloudef 提到了Kaze Emanuar的视频“Optimizing with Bad Code”，该视频也简要介绍了自修改代码。
• [技术研究] @xixixao 研究了macOS上可执行文件在ARM架构下的表现，特别关注增量编译的性能优化，指出在macOS上通过JIT进行页面重映射是当前实现该目标的唯一方法，但存在挑战。
• [潜在优化] @alcover 认为自修改代码可能在运行时优化中带来巨大好处，尽管调试难度很大。
• [格式赞赏] @oxcabe 对某篇文章的排版和内容组织表示赞赏，认为其结构清晰，有助于理解复杂的技术内容。

补充讨论：
• [Common Lisp视角] @pfdietz 指出在Common Lisp中，生成、编译和执行新代码的程序并不特殊，可以通过构建lambda表达式并调用编译函数来实现。
• [系统限制] @belter 提出在OpenBSD中，由于W^X（Write Xor Execute）机制，自修改代码可能无法工作。
• [技术质疑与细节] @Someone 对某篇文章中自修改代码示例的可靠性提出质疑，指出其在多个方面（如架构依赖、编译器优化、指令缓存处理等）存在潜在问题，并提出为何示例中未处理指令缓存刷新问题。

争议焦点：
• 自修改代码在不同平台和系统上的可行性和限制，例如在OpenBSD上的W^X机制下的不可行性。
• 自修改代码示例的技术细节和假设的可靠性，特别是在不同编译器优化和系统环境下的表现。

44089106.article_content:
âWhy would you ever want to write a program that changes its code while itâs running? Thatâs a horrible idea!â
Yes, yes it is. Itâs a good learning experience though. This is not something you would ever do outside of exploring a curiosity.
Self-mutating/self-modifying programs arenât useful for a whole lot. They make for difficult debugging, the program becomes hardware dependent, and the code is extremely tedious and confusing to read unless you are an expert assembly programmer. The only good use for self-mutating programs in the wild I know of is as a cloaking mechanism for malware. My goal is purely academic so I venture into nothing of the sort here.
Warning: This post is heavy on x86_64 assembly of which I am no expert. A fair amount of research went into writing this and itâs possible (almost expected) that mistakes were made. If you find one, send an email so that it may be corrected.
The first step of writing a self-mutating program is being able to change the code at runtime. Programmers figured out long ago that this was a bad idea and since then protections have been added to prevent a programâs code from being changed at runtime. We first need to understand where the programâs instructions live when the program is being executed. When a program is to be executed, the loader will load the entire program into memory. The program then executes inside of a virtual address space that is managed by the kernel. This address space is broken up into different segments as illustrated below.
In this case, weâre only concerned with the text segment. This is where the instructions of the process are stored. Behind the address space are pages which are handled by the kernel. These pages map to the physical memory of the computer. The kernel controls permissions to each of these pages. By default, the text segment pages are set to read and execute. You may not write to them. In order to change the instructions at runtime, weâll need to change the permissions of the text segment pages so that we write to them.
Changing the permissions of a page can be done with the
mprotect()
function. The only tricky part of
mprotect()
is that the pointer you give it must be aligned to a page boundary. Here is a function that given a pointer, moves the pointer to the page boundary and then changes that page to read, write, and execute permissions.

If we give this function a pointer that points to an address in the text segment, that page in the text segment will now be writeable. It is important to note that the OS may refuse to allow the text segment to be writeable. Iâm working on Linux, which does allow for writing to the text segment. If you are using another OS, make sure youâre checking the return value to see if the call to
mprotect()
failed. In the examples below, we assume that the function weâll be changing is contained entirely on a single page. For long functions, this may not be the case.
Now that we can write to the text segment, the next question is: what do we write?
Letâs start with something simple. Say I have the following function:

data.title: Writing your own CUPS printer driver in 100 lines of Python (2018)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Pretix 1.8版本引入了邮件寄送管理功能，允许将高质门票通过平邮寄送给客户，而非提供下载。此功能特别适合需要高质量门票的场景，如礼品或纪念品。为实现此功能，需使用热敏票据打印机和专用票纸。文章对比了BOCA Lemur和Practical Automation uITL+2003CF两款打印机，最终选择了更实惠的uITL+。然而，uITL+仅支持Windows驱动，而BOCA支持多平台。由于FGL协议的限制和驱动的兼容性问题，要在Linux系统上使用uITL+，需自行开发驱动。文章详细介绍了通过CUPS系统开发过滤器程序“rastertofgl”的步骤，将光栅数据转换为FGL代码，以实现打印功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CUPS打印系统及其在不同场景下的应用和问题

不同观点：
• 作者[_rami_]提到，他们现在主要使用原装的Boca打印机和官方驱动，且99%的打印任务来自Android设备，CUPS已经不再使用。不过，他回顾过去使用CUPS的经历时认为那是一段有趣的体验。

• [roywashere]提到Pretix这个开源软件，并对其开发票据打印机驱动表示赞赏。
• [saltcured]回顾了自己早期使用C语言和Ghostview插件系统在Linux上打印的经历。
• [dale_huevo]认为CUPS驱动必须用C语言编写是一个误解，并指出许多廉价的热敏打印机附带的预编译二进制驱动不仅违反GPL协议，还可能包含恶意软件。
• [th0ma5]分享了一个有趣的案例，利用CUPS让一台旧的Commodore 64打印机重新工作。
• [whycome]提问是否有专门用于此类场景的大语言模型（LLM）。

争议焦点：
- 使用第三方驱动程序的合法性问题，尤其是BOCA驱动程序的许可证限制（[userbinator]的观点）。
- 热敏打印机使用中健康和安全问题，特别是纸张中含有的化学物质（[Havoc]的观点）。

总体来看，讨论围绕CUPS系统的技术实现、实际应用中的问题、健康与安全考量以及开源软件和驱动的法律问题展开。

In
version 1.8
of pretix, we introduced shipping
management as a new feature for the pretix Hosted and Enterprise editions. With this plug-in, you can choose not to
deliver your tickets to your visitors as a downloadable file, but to send them via snail mail instead. Of course,
you can just download those tickets as regular-sized PDF files, print them out and ship them, but the feature is
usually most interesting if you want to send out high-quality tickets that look good e.g. in a gift wrapping under
a christmas tree or pinned to a wall as a souvenier of the event.
For this purpose, you will need a thermal ticket printer as well as suitable ticket paper. Last year, I took a closer
look at this market and tested devices from two of the major ticket printer vendors: The
BOCA Lemur
as well as the
Practical Automation uITL+2003CF
model.
In our test, the printing quality of both printers was very similar. The uITL+ is missing a network port in contrast to the
BOCA Lemur, but the uITL+ features a nicer case (smaller and metal instead of plastic) and is way more affordable to obtain,
at least here in Europe.
For this reason, we chose the uITL+ as our reference printer and for our first customer installation. You’ve already
seen a photo of the uITL+ in our last blogpost:
However, there is another downside to the uITL+: It only comes with a Windows driver, while the BOCA printers come with
drivers for all platforms, including
packages
for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora,
CentOS, Arch Linux, FreeBSD, and even an ARM build for the Raspberry Pi.
Both printers speak FGL (“Friendly Ghost Language”) over the wire, a communication protocol common to the world
of ticketing printers. With FGL, you can send ASCII text and style information in order to render your tickets directly
on the printer (but we want to send PDFs rendered on the server instead, which is why we need a driver to convert).
Documentations of FGL can be obtained via the websites of
both
vendors
. This also means that the drivers are, in
theory, cross-compatible with minimal adjustments in configuration.
However, the license of the BOCA driver forbids using their driver to control printers of other vendors. Additionally, no
sources of the driver are available and some builds (like the ARM build of the Raspberry Pi package) only run on very old operating systems
since they link to very old library versions.
Therefore, to use the uITL+ from a Linux operating system, we need to roll our own driver.
Printing on unix-like operating systems like Linux or macOS is usually done through the
CUPS
daemon. CUPS is responsible for handling printer configuration, scheduling print jobs and actually talking to the printer
over the wire. Unfortunately, though, CUPS does not speak FGL out of the box.
If we look into CUPS’
documentation on driver development
, we see that we
basically need to work on two tasks:
We need to write a filter program that takes rastered pixel data as an input and outputs FGL code.
We need to generate a
PPD file
that contains configuration
information about the printer (i.e. name, name of the newly created filter, paper sizes, cutter settings).
Writing a CUPS filter
Let’s get started with writing our CUPS filter, which we will call
rastertofgl
. Usually, most CUPS filters are written
in C, but I decided to choose Python instead – not only because I know it better, but also because writing it in a compiled
language also means that we need to cross-compile it to different architectures like ARM if we want to run it on devices
like the Raspberry Pi, which creates additional effort. Basically, we can use any language because the filter just needs
to be an executable that reads a data stream on standard input and outputs a data stream on standard output.
The incoming data stream consists of pages of data in the
CUPS Raster Format
,
version 3. Every page starts with a page header of fixed length containing meta information such as the color space, page
size, orientation, etc. In order to be able to conveniently access this data later, let’s start by defining a
namedtuple
for storage. For brevity, I’m not including all the 104 properties here:
CupsRas3
=
namedtuple
(
'CupsRas3'
,
'MediaClass MediaColor MediaType OutputType AdvanceDistance '
'AdvanceMedia Collate CutMedia Duplex HWResolutionH '
'HWResolutionV ImagingBoundingBoxL ImagingBoundingBoxB '
'ImagingBoundingBoxR ImagingBoundingBoxT InsertSheet Jog '
'LeadingEdge MarginsL MarginsB ManualFeed MediaPosition'
...
)
Next, we make use of the
struct
module from Python’s standard library
to read the magic word from the beginning and then split the binary stream into all its different components. From the
header, we then know the width and height of the page in pixels as well as the number of bits per pixels, allowing us to
read all of the page into a bytearray and then continuing with parsing the next page:
def
read_ras3
(
rdata
):
if
not
rdata
:
raise
ValueError
(
'No data received'
)
# Check for magic word (eithe
44088682.article_summary: Pretix 1.8版本引入了邮件寄送管理功能，允许将高质门票通过平邮寄送给客户，而非提供下载。此功能特别适合需要高质量门票的场景，如礼品或纪念品。为实现此功能，需使用热敏票据打印机和专用票纸。文章对比了BOCA Lemur和Practical Automation uITL+2003CF两款打印机，最终选择了更实惠的uITL+。然而，uITL+仅支持Windows驱动，而BOCA支持多平台。由于FGL协议的限制和驱动的兼容性问题，要在Linux系统上使用uITL+，需自行开发驱动。文章详细介绍了通过CUPS系统开发过滤器程序“rastertofgl”的步骤，将光栅数据转换为FGL代码，以实现打印功能。

data.title: Lisping at JPL (2002)
data.author: adityaathalye
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了Lisp语言在喷气推进实验室（JPL）的兴衰历程，重点描述了1988年至1991年期间，作者参与自主移动机器人项目的工作经历。当时，JPL正在规划火星探测任务，大型探测器是主流，但作者的导师David Miller主张使用小型探测器，并通过创意筹资雇佣了Colin Angle开发小型机器人Tooth，与大型的Robby形成对比。Lisp是当时AI开发的主要语言，Robby和Tooth都使用Lisp编程。尽管Robby运行Lisp，但Tooth由于内存限制，使用了专门的Lisp编译器生成6811代码。后来，作者开发了ALFA语言，用于编程Rocky系列机器人，最终应用于火星探路者任务的Sojourner探测器（该探测器改用C语言编程）。尽管这段时间JPL在机器人研究上取得显著成果，但由于组织内部斗争，机器人智能小组最终解散，大部分成员离开。

• [hatmatrix]认为，Lisp在早期选择中非常有意义，但2001-2004年后，其他主流语言在团队协作和维护遗留代码库方面更有优势，尽管他本人是Lisp的粉丝。
• [adityaathalye]引用了1994-1999年期间远程代理调试的故事，强调了Lisp在特定应用场景中的独特价值。
• [adamgordonbell]提供了一个包含图片的版本链接，展示了对Ron Garrett的采访，进一步介绍了Lisp在JPL的历史。

总体而言，讨论围绕Lisp的历史应用、当前状态及其在现代环境中的潜在价值展开，参与者提供了不同的视角和个人经验。

44059994.article_content:
Lisping at JPL
Copyright (c) 2002 by Ron Garret
(
f.k.a. Erann Gat
),
all rights reserved.
This is the story of the rise and fall of Lisp at the Jet Propulsion
Lab as told from my personal (and highly biased) point of view.  I am
not writing in my official capacity as an employee of JPL, nor am I in
any way representing the official position of JPL.  (This will become
rather obvious shortly.)
1988-1991 - The Robotics Years
I came to JPL in 1988 to work in the Artificial Intelligence group on
autonomous mobile robots.  Times were different then.  Dollars flowed
more freely from government coffers.  AI Winter was just beginning, and
it had not yet arrived at JPL.  (Technology at the Lab tends to run a
few years behind the state of the art :-)
JPL at the time was in the early planning stages for a Mars rover
mission called Mars Rover Sample Return (MRSR).  In those days space
missions were Big, with a capital B.  The MRSR rover was to weigh nearly
a ton.  The mission budget was going to be in the billions of dollars
(which was typical in those days).
Against this backdrop I went to work for a fellow named
David Miller
,
who also happened to be my thesis advisor.  Dave had the then-radical
idea of using small rovers to explore planets instead of big ones.  In
1988 that was a tough sell.  Very few people believed that a small rover
could do anything useful.  (Many still don't.)
Using some creatively acquired R&D funding, Dave hired Colin Angle (then
a grad student working for Rod Brooks at MIT, now CEO of IS Robotics) as
a summer student.  Colin built
a small robot named Tooth
,
which stood in very stark contrast to the 2000-pound
Robby
,
which was the testbed for the MRSR mission.
At the time it was more or less taken for granted that AI work was done
in Lisp.  C++ barely existed.  Perl was brand new.  Java was years away.
Spacecraft were mostly programmed in assembler, or, if you were really
being radical, Ada.
Robby had two Motorola 68020 processors running vxWorks, each with (if
memory serves) 8 MB of RAM.  (This was considered a huge amount of RAM
in those days.  In fact, the Robby work was often criticized for, among
other things, being too memory-hungry to be of any use.)  Tooth, by
contrast, had two Motorola 68hc11 8-bit microcontrollers each with 256
bytes of RAM and 2k bytes of EEPROM.  (In later robots we used 6811's
with a whopping 32k bytes of RAM.)
(As an indication of just how fast and how radically attitudes can
change, the other day I heard an engineer complain that "you can't
do
anything
with only 128 megabytes.")
Both Robby and Tooth were programmed using Lisp.  On Robby we actually
ran Lisp on-board.  The Lisp we used was
T 3.1
which was ported
from a Sun3 to vxWorks with a great deal of help from Jim Firby, who
came to JPL from Yale.  Jim also wrote a T-in-common-lisp compatibility
package called Common T.  Using Common T we could do code
development on a Macintosh (using Macintosh Common Lisp and a Robbie
simulator, also written by Jim) and then run the resulting code directly
on Robby with no changes.
Tooth's processors didn't have nearly enough RAM to run Lisp directly
[1]
so instead we used a custom-designed compiler
written in Lisp to generate 6811 code.  At first we used Rod Brooks's
subsumption compiler, but later I decided I didn't like the constraints
imposed by the subsumption architecture and wrote my own for a language
called ALFA
[2]
.  ALFA was subsequently used to
program a whole series of rovers, the
Rocky series
, which
eventually led to the
Sojourner
rover
on the Mars Pathfinder mission. (Sojourner had an Intel 8085
processor with 1 MB of bank-switched RAM.  It was programmed in C.  More
on this decision later.)
Tooth, Robby, and the Rocky series were among the most capable robots of
their day.  Robby was the first robot ever to navigate autonomously in
an outdoor environment using stereo vision as its only sensor.  (NOTE:
The stereo vision code was written in C by Larry Matthies.)
Tooth was only the second robot to do an indoor object-collection task,
the other being
Herbert
, which
was developed a year or two earlier in by Jonathan Connell working in
Rod Brooks's mobot lab at MIT.  (But Tooth was vastly more reliable than
Herbert.) The Rocky robots were the first ever microrovers to operate
successfully in rough-terrain environments.  In 1990,
Rocky III
demonstrated a fully autonomous traverse and sample collection mission,
a capability that has not been reproduced to my knowledge in the twelve
years since.
The period between 1988 and 1991 was amazingly productive for autonomous
mobile robot work at JPL.  It was also, unfortunately, politically
turbulent.  Dave Miller's group was, alas, not part of the
organizational structure that had the "official" charter for doing
robotics research at JPL.  The result was a bloody turf battle, whose
eventual result was the dissolution of the Robotic Intelligence group,
and the departure of nearly all of its members (and, probably, the

data.title: The Newark airport crisis
data.article_summary: 文章指出，纽瓦克机场正面临严重的空中交通管制危机，这不仅是局部问题，而是可能影响整个航空系统。主要原因包括空中交通管制员短缺、IT管理不善、技术过时等。2024年，美国空域的航班数量创纪录，而FAA仍在使用1990年代初设计的过时系统，难以应对日益增长的航班数量。纽瓦克机场多次出现雷达和通讯中断，最严重的一次导致所有雷达屏幕变黑，航班被迫暂停，造成大量航班取消和延误。虽然未发生事故，但系统脆弱性和安全隐患显而易见。文章警告，若不尽快解决，危机将影响更多机场，导致更大范围的航班混乱。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

A shortage of air traffic controllers, bungled IT management, outdated technology, and a brewing disaster in our airspace.

The Newark airport crisis is about to become everyone’s problem
A shortage of air traffic controllers, bungled IT management, outdated technology, and a brewing disaster in our airspace.
by
Darryl Campbell
May 25, 2025, 12:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission.
See our ethics statement.
There are too many planes in the sky. In 2024, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) supervised nearly
16.8 million
flights in American airspace — half a million more than the year prior. To manage all of those airplanes, however, the FAA uses an air traffic control system
designed in the early 1990s
— when features like trackballs and color monitors were new, and air traffic controllers handled less than
half as many flights every year
.
Like many government agencies, the FAA has faced
chronic budget constraints and poor oversight
in the ensuing two decades. Not only is its system functionally obsolete; it’s also badly understaffed. Too often, the agency must scramble to find the least-bad solution for its mounting problems —
and not all of these solutions are good or even safe
.
One such scenario has been unfolding at Newark Liberty International Airport for the last year. And it hasn’t just created delays and cancellations — it has put people’s safety at risk.
A screen displaying flight status is seen at Newark Liberty International Airport in Newark, New Jersey on May 7, 2025.
AFP via Getty Images
Outages
Newark airport became national news starting on Monday, April 28th. Around 1:27PM, pilots abruptly lost contact with the controllers that oversee the airport’s approach and departure airspace, known as Newark Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON).
“
Can you hear us
?” asked one United pilot. After a beat of silence, another pilot keyed the radio. “Hey Approach, are you there?” A third chimed in, his call sign more of a question. “Austrian eight-niner?”
Several more seconds passed before Newark TRACON came back on the air.
“United 1951, how do you hear me?”
“Loud and clear now,” the first pilot replied.
“Hey Approach, are you there?”
For the moment, normal operations resumed — though controllers were worried about the possibility of another outage. “Upjet 905, join the final approach course,” said one controller, then prudently added, “if you don’t hear me, you can continue on the approach.”
Seconds later, every radar screen at Newark approach went dark.
“
Radar contact lost. We just lost our radar
.”
Suddenly blind and unsure if they could even maintain comms with pilots, Newark’s controllers did what they were trained to do — get everyone to a safe holding place until the situation stabilized. To one United pilot in final descent: “stay on the arrival and maintain 6000.”
To a private pilot, also preparing to land: “climb and maintain 4500.” They diverted another private pilot off to a nearby small airport: “Continue on towards Caldwell, call Caldwell Tower 119.8.” And they told a fourth private pilot passing that it was now up to him to maintain visual separation from other aircraft: “we’re just gonna have to cut you loose.”
‘Disruption is significant’
Air traffic controllers prepare for such contingencies, according to Dr. Hassan Shahidi, the president and CEO of the nonprofit FlightSafety Foundation.
“Emergency traffic is prioritized,” he said. “Flights may be held on the ground. Nearby centers may take over some services.”
Even in the best-case scenarios, however, “disruption is significant.”
Controllers at Newark only lost radio and radar for about a minute and a half until backup systems kicked in. And no airplanes crashed or even had a near miss. But it took the rest of the afternoon just to get operations restarted. No one took off again until
5PM
, more than three hours later. At least a dozen flights were canceled, and 30 others were diverted to nearby airports. Higher-than-normal delays persisted for
more than a week after the outage
as airlines dealt with planes and crews that were out of position.
Another outage occurred a week and a half later on May 9th. At 3:55AM, radar displays went out
twice
.
“
Imma hand you off here, our scopes just went black again
,” said one of the controllers as she passed one flight over to JFK and LaGuardia controllers, who still had radar. “If you care about this, contact your airline and try to get some pressure on them to fix this stuff.”
“Imma hand you off here, our scopes just went black again.”
She was right to be exasperated. This was the
sixth time
in only
nine month

data.title: Plwm – An X11 window manager written in Prolog
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary: **plwm** 是一个用 Prolog 编写的 X11 窗口管理器，具有高度可定制性，专注于动态平铺窗口管理。其主要特点包括易于配置和修改，使用声明式的 Prolog 语言进行设置；支持多种平铺布局和浮动窗口；轻量级，内存占用仅10-15MB；支持多显示器、外部状态栏（如 polybar）、工作区动态操作等功能。安装需依赖 Xorg 和 SWI-Prolog，通过修改 `.xinitrc` 文件或使用显示管理器配置启动。用户可通过 Prolog 代码定义窗口行为，实现高度个性化的窗口管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Prolog语言在实际项目中的应用及其在窗口管理器中的使用

不同观点：
• raron认为Prolog在教程和实际项目中的应用差别很大，从简单的例子过渡到复杂项目时会遇到无限递归和无法解决的问题，表明Prolog在实际应用中的难度。
• eikenberry希望有人能为Wayland写一个窗口管理服务，用协议取代合成器API，以便用任何语言实现窗口管理器。
• major505对Prolog在实际项目中的使用表示惊讶，尤其是用来写窗口管理器，并对Prolog的一般使用表示质疑。
• Jerry2关注是否有用JS和CSS实现的窗口管理器，或允许使用这些技术进行窗口管理和装饰的窗口管理器。
• rabiescow用幽默的方式批评一些人坚持使用X11，而不愿接受新的变化。
• 5-作为Prolog的外行，质疑该项目是否真正利用了Prolog的逻辑特性，或者只是使用了其功能性子集，并讨论了Prolog作为非逻辑功能语言的优点。
• smikhanov对项目源代码的简洁表示赞赏。
• YeGoblynQueenne对项目的文档和整体印象表示赞赏，并有意尝试。
• bolangi对与plwm类似的窗口管理器感兴趣，希望了解其灵感来源。
• jimmaswell在Gentoo上安装并编译了项目，但遇到问题，只得到一个鼠标光标和黑色屏幕。
• B1FF_PSUVM提到这让他想起全Erlang的HN首页，可能暗示对特定语言项目的兴趣或趋势。
• leephillips对项目的实现表示赞赏，但指出由于其使用工作区而非标签，不能替代dwm。
• gatane开玩笑地建议用Scheme实现一个类似的项目。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及Prolog在实际项目中的挑战和复杂性，以及对不同编程语言和技术的偏好和应用场景的讨论。
• 对窗口管理器的实现技术及其可用性的关注，尤其是对JS和CSS等web技术的兴趣。
• 对开源项目文档和代码简洁性的赞赏，以及在实际安装和使用中遇到的具体问题。
• 对不同窗口管理器的功能和设计理念的比较和评价。

About
plwm is a highly customizable X11 dynamic tiling window manager written in
Prolog
.
Main goals of the project are: high code & documentation quality; powerful yet easy customization; covering most common needs of tiling WM users; and to stay small, easy to use and hack on.
Powered by
SWI-Prolog
Feature highlights
Easy to hack on, great way to introduce yourself to the logic programming paradigm and Prolog
Easy to configure: Prolog is declarative, so even though the config is source code, it feels like a dedicated format
Tiling is dynamic, with various layouts included by default: monocle, vertical/horizontal stacks, grid, left/right/top/bottom/centered master-stack, nrows(N), ncols(N)
Floating windows are also supported (move/resize with mouse)
Support for external bars, e.g. polybar, lemonbar
Nice level of EWMH compilance -
partially still work-in-progress
Performance: plwm is fast and light as a feather when it comes to resource usage (10-15 MB memory)
Dynamic workspace operations: create, rename, reindex or delete workspaces on the fly
Other features: multi-monitor support, inner/outer gaps, menu integrations with dmenu/rofi, rules, hooks, animations, command fifo and more
You can say: "My window manager is a semantic consequence of a set of axioms and implications which my computer is deducing/proving from an infinitely branching proof-tree"
Installation
Dependencies:
xorg
with
libx11-dev
,
libxft-dev
,
libxrandr-dev
(exact package names may vary)
SWI-Prolog
(downloadable from most distros' package repos)
On Ubuntu 22.04, easiest way to install them is:
$ sudo apt install xorg-dev swi-prolog
Run:
$ make && sudo make install
By default, this will install plwm to
/usr/local/bin/
. The location can be adjusted in the
Makefile
.
Minimal environment
Add the following line to the end of your
~/.xinitrc
:
exec plwm
Then simply use the command
startx
in tty.
For example, to automate this after logging in, put these lines in
~/.bash_profile
(or to whatever shell startup that matches your setup):
#
Start X from login shell on tty1 if not already started
if
[
-z
"
$DISPLAY
"
-a
$(
tty
)
=
"
/dev/tty1
"
]
;
then
exec
startx
fi
Using a display manager
Please refer to the documentation of your display manager on how to set up sessions for custom WMs.
Here
you can find good references for this.
For most modern display managers, you'll have to create a
/usr/share/xsessions/plwm.desktop
file with content like:
[Desktop Entry]
Name
=plwm
Comment
=This session logs you into plwm
Exec
=plwm
Icon
=path-to-this-repo/plwm/img/logo.png
Type
=Application
Usage
Basics
Command-line options are listed by running
plwm -h
. The manual plwm(1) also contains them as well as the default keybindings.
If you have already used dynamic tiling WMs like dwm, then nothing should be too surprising in this section.
All windows are
managed
by default. This means that whenever a window spawns, it will be added to a list. We call this list the
stack
. Also, the placement and the size of the windows are automatically calculated and set. This is determined by the currently active
layout
(stack, horizontal stack, grid, etc.).
Some layouts are called "master-stack" layouts (the ones which have "master" in their names, e.g.,
lmaster
). With these layouts the first
nmaster
number of windows (1 by default) in the stack go to a dedicated area. These are the
master windows
, which usually have the most space allocated for them. All other windows go to the remaining screen space.
For example, if you start plwm with the default config, you have:
layout = lmaster
,
nmaster = 1
,
mfact = 2/3
, which means that the stack's top window will always be on the left side and occupy 2/3 of the screen width, while the other windows will be in a secondary stack on the right having 1/3 of the screen width.
Some base promises of this approach:
Declarative window management: you only
tell
your system
what
window arrangement you want and don't do the movement/resizin

data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了美国历史上的关税发展。关税是最早的税收形式之一，因易于征收而被广泛使用，但也引发了走私等逃税行为。在美国殖民时期，罗德岛因地理优势成为走私中心，并反对任何压制走私的尝试，是最早宣布脱离英国的殖民地，且最晚批准宪法。1789年宪法生效后，亚历山大·汉密尔顿作为首任财政部长，通过关税和消费税等措施改善了国家财政，关税收入成为联邦政府的主要收入来源。最初关税仅为增加财政收入，但后来也被用于保护国内产业，尤其是在美国工业革命开始后，纺织业的发展推动了对保护性关税的需求。新英格兰地区因水力资源丰富，成为纺织业中心，并在1812年战争后几乎垄断了美国市场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： tariffs（关税）的有效性、历史先例、当前实施情况及其经济影响

不同观点：
• **支持关税的观点**：
  - SSJPython指出，历史上如美国、德国和日本通过有针对性的关税和补贴成功促进了国内产业发展。例如，美国在亚历山大·汉密尔顿的“美国体系”下使用关税来保护新兴产业，德国和日本也采取了类似政策并成为经济强国。
  - 这些国家通过设定出口目标（KPI）来确保受补贴企业能够在国际市场上竞争，最终实现自给自足。
  
• **质疑关税有效性的观点**：
  - kiitos和tzs认为，关税并非德美汽车市场份额差异的主要原因，而是产品质量等其他因素在起作用。例如，德国汽车在美国市场更受欢迎是因为其质量较高，而不是关税的结果。
  - mustache_kimono指出，虽然历史上有关税成功的例子，但当前缺乏经济计量学的支持，且关税可能误导公众。例如，日本对美国汽车实行0%关税，但日本消费者仍然不购买美国车。
  
• **关注关税对知识产权和全球贸易的影响**：
  - mmastrac认为，关税讨论忽略了全球对美国知识产权的尊重，这种尊重是全球贸易体系的重要组成部分。如果全球贸易崩溃，美国长期积累的财富可能受到威胁。
  
• **关税的政治与经济自由讨论**：
  - resters强烈反对关税，认为关税是政治干预经济自由的体现，限制了公民的选择权。相较于中国有针对性的产业政策，美国的关税政策显得情绪化和反复无常，且最终伤害了美国经济。
  
• **对当前美国关税政策的批评**：
  - archagon和coliveira隐晦地提到关税讨论中可能存在宣传和误导信息，暗示当前的讨论缺乏客观性。
  - brightball指出，历史讨论中忽略了关税背后的复杂背景，例如萨姆特堡的存在不仅仅是为了关税收集。

补充讨论：
• **历史先例与当前政策的关联**：
  - saravanan2661和throw0101d提到历史上通过“借鉴”他国技术实现工业化的例子，以及特定情况下关税可能有效的背景，但这些历史案例与当前政策的直接关联性受到质疑。
  
• **对讨论内容的形式批评**：
  - profsummergig和djeastm对缺乏数据支持和参考文献的文章表示不满，认为这样的讨论缺乏严谨性。

争议焦点：
• 关税在历史上成功促进经济发展的案例是否能直接应用于当前复杂的全球经济环境。
• 关税政策的实施是否更多出于政治和情绪考量，而非基于严谨的经济分析。
• 产品质量、消费者偏好等非关税因素在国际贸易中的作用是否被关税讨论忽视。

44080237.article_content:
May 2025 | Volume 54, Issue 5
Tariffs in American History
John Steele Gordon
Author,
An Empire of Wealth: The Epic History of American Economic Power
The following is adapted from a lecture delivered in Washington, D.C., on May 6, 2025, as part of the AWC Family Foundation Lecture Series. Sponsored by Hillsdale College’s Allan P. Kirby, Jr. Center for Constitutional Studies and Citizenship, which is undergoing extensive expansion and renovation, the lecture was delivered in The Heritage Foundation’s Van Andel–Gaby Center.
Tariffs are among the oldest of taxes for the simple reason that they are easy to collect. Just send in the tax collectors and don’t let the goods being transported move until the duty has been paid. Being one of the earliest forms of taxation, it is not surprising that tariffs produced one of the earliest forms of tax evasion: smuggling.
In America’s colonial period, the east coast of the United States, with its many rivers and inlets that the small ships of those days could utilize, lent itself to smuggling, and the American colonists evaded British tariffs on a grand scale.
Indeed, Rhode Island, with its long coastline relative to the area and its many small harbors, was the epicenter of colonial smuggling, and it opposed any attempts to suppress it. Rhode Island was the first colony to foreswear allegiance to Great Britain, on May 4, 1776, two months before the Declaration of Independence. It was also the only state not to send delegates to the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia in 1787, fearing that a stronger federal government, empowered to tax, would suppress smuggling. And it was the last state to ratify the Constitution, on May 29, 1790, more than a year after the federal government had come into existence. It did so then only under the threat of having its exports taxed as if from a foreign nation.
When the Constitution took effect in 1789, the first order of business was to straighten out the nation’s disastrous financial situation. That is why the new State Department started out with only five employees while the Treasury Department had 40.
When Alexander Hamilton became the nation’s first Secretary of the Treasury, he immediately began to prepare a schedule of tariffs, along with excise taxes on such commodities as alcohol and tobacco. The Constitution forbids taxing the exports of any state, and so American tariffs have always been laid only on imports.
Collectors were named for each port, and these were considered plum jobs because the collector got to keep the money, earning interest on it, until it was forwarded to the federal government a few times a year.
Hamilton’s tariffs, along with the refunding of the national debt and the establishment of a central bank, transformed the American financial situation. By the end of the 1790s, the U.S. had the best credit rating in Europe, its bonds selling over par. By 1800, federal revenues, a mere $3.7 million in 1792, had nearly tripled to $10.8 million. About 90 percent of that revenue came from tariffs—a ratio that wouldn’t change much, except during the Civil War, for more than a century.
***
Hamilton’s tariffs had been solely for the purpose of raising revenue. But, of course, there is another use to which tariffs can be put: the protection of domestic industries from foreign competition.
In 1789, except for shipbuilding, there had been little American industry to protect. At his first inauguration, George Washington had been symbolically careful to wear a suit made of cloth woven in the U.S. rather than from cloth imported from Britain, as almost all high-quality cloth was at that time.
Britain was where the industrial spinning and weaving technology was, and Britain was determined to keep it there. Textile machinery, as well as plans for it, could not be exported—and those with expertise in the industry were not allowed to emigrate. This problem (when seen from an American viewpoint) was solved through industrial espionage. Samuel Slater, who had apprenticed in the cloth industry and had a marked talent for mechanics, carefully memorized the needed plans for spinning and weaving machinery and sailed to America, having listed himself as a farmhand on the ship’s manifest.
Within a year, using capital from Rhode Island’s Brown family (for whom Brown University is named), Slater had a spinning mill in operation. The American Industrial Revolution had begun—and with it a push for protective tariffs.
New England, with its many clear-running streams and rivers to provide waterpower, soon had a flourishing spinning industry, whereas the weaving of cloth was still initially done at home. But in 1814, Francis Cabot Lowell built a factory that would merge spinning and weaving into the first fully integrated cloth mill in the world.

data.title: SteamOS now released officially for any device
data.author: cultofmetatron
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Steam平台的主要功能和版块。Steam是一个提供各类游戏、软件和多媒体内容的在线商店和社区平台。用户可以通过"Discovery Queue"和"Wishlist"发现和跟踪新内容，"Community"版块提供讨论、市场和创意工坊等互动功能。平台还提供各种游戏分类和主题选择，支持不同语言和设备，如Steam Deck和VR硬件。此外，Steam定期举办促销活动和特别活动，如Steam Replay和Steam Next Fest。用户还可以获得玩家支持，处理如合作模式、多人游戏和单人模式等问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SteamOS的设备兼容性及安装可行性

不同观点：
• ruytlm认为当前SteamOS并没有真正实现对任何设备的兼容，但他个人在一些旧硬件上通过Bazzite项目成功实现了与电视的连接使用，暗示对非官方支持设备的探索。
• Bender指出，目前SteamOS仅官方支持Steam Deck和Legion Go S等特定设备，但提到最近更新的Steam和SteamOS提升了与其他基于AMD的PC手持设备的兼容性，并鼓励用户通过SteamOS恢复镜像进行测试和反馈。
• sagarm强调当前SteamOS的支持非常有限，主要面向AMD硬件和NVME驱动的手持设备，排除了在ARM架构设备上运行的可能性。
• gnabgib提供了一个指向Hacker News的讨论链接，暗示该话题在其他平台上也引发了大量讨论。
• throwaway314155认为相关新闻标题具有误导性，但同时表示这是一个好消息，反映出对SteamOS扩展兼容性的潜在期待。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于SteamOS的实际兼容范围与官方宣称的范围不符。部分用户期待更广泛的设备支持，特别是对非AMD设备和ARM架构设备的支持。
• 用户ruytlm和Bender提供了非官方解决方案，如Bazzite项目和SteamOS恢复镜像，展示了社区对扩大设备兼容性的积极探索。
• Hacker News上的广泛讨论表明该话题在技术社区中引起了较大关注，可能反映出用户对SteamOS未来发展的关注和期望。
