data.title: Lieferando.de has captured 5.7% of restaurant related domain names
data.author: __natty__
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何利用Common Crawl项目的数据，通过简单的命令行和bash脚本，收集了约900万个德国“.de”域名。作者特别关注餐厅相关的域名，通过筛选与餐厅有关的德语词汇，最终得到约3.1万个餐厅域名。为验证这些域名的有效性，作者使用了PowerShell和Golang程序，发现其中63%仍活跃，49%存在重定向，14%仍使用http协议，37%已失效。进一步分析显示，其中5.7%的活跃域名被Lieferando.de捕获，显示了该平台通过捕获域名进行流量引导的激进策略。作者推测，这反映了2019-2023年间德国餐厅行业的困境，并暗示这种策略可能有效且成本低廉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：餐厅遭遇域名劫持和电话劫持的问题，在线平台的不道德商业行为，以及对当前互联网域名系统和在线存在的反思。

不同观点：
• TrackerFF 描述了一个餐厅老板遇到电话和网站劫持的问题。有人篡改了餐厅的电话和网站信息，导致客户无法联系到餐厅。当餐厅老板付费给某个公司后，电话和订单恢复正常，但停止付费后问题重现。这揭示了小型企业面对这种不道德商业行为时的困境。

• reustle 提到美国的外卖平台 GrubHub 也做过类似的事情，注册了大量域名并在谷歌地图上未经许可列出餐厅信息。这表明该问题不仅限于某个地区或公司，而是一个更为普遍的现象。

• ctxc 补充说，这些公司不仅创建假网站，还通过这些网站声称拥有谷歌地图的列表，然后勒索餐厅支付费用来修正信息。

• quaintdev 提出了一个更为广泛的讨论，认为当前的DNS系统和网站模型对普通用户过于复杂，很多人尤其是发展中国家的企业主更倾向于使用WhatsApp和社交媒体来进行在线营销。这揭示了传统互联网寻址系统的用户体验问题，并建议需要重新思考互联网的可发现性和身份问题。

• mousetree 批评 Lieferando 花费精力在注册域名上而不是改进应用，并指出其在柏林的糟糕服务体验。

• exiguus 建议将这种不道德行为曝光给媒体，以提高公众 awareness。

• ahmedfromtunis 提出小型餐厅可以通过先拥有域名来进行品牌重塑，尽管这并不是理想的解决方案。

• kleiba 指出这种行为可能已经违反了现有法律，但小型餐厅往往没有能力与大公司打官司。

• miohtama 提到越来越多的小型餐厅只做Facebook页面，避免复杂的网站管理，但这也导致了依赖中心化平台的问题。

• c16 调侃了Takeaway公司缺乏EEAT（专家经验、权威性、可信赖性），并建议谷歌应介入处理这种滥用行为。

• nubinetwork 怀疑 Doordash 也有类似行为，将讨论扩展到其他可能存在相同问题的公司。

• postepowanieadm 简单评论了德国法律系统的古怪，没有详细展开。

• weinzierl 提到亚马逊在早期也注册了大量域名，尽管数量上可能不如当代的域名抢注者。

• josefrichter 质疑域名在2025年的重要性，认为现在人们不再通过输入域名访问网站，因此域名的实际价值可能有限。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于餐厅老板面对的在线平台不道德行为，包括域名劫持和电话劫持，以及他们在面对这种行为时的无力感。
• 讨论中还涉及到对当前互联网寻址和在线存在系统的反思，有人认为DNS和传统网站模型对普通用户过于复杂，建议寻找更直观的方式。
• 社交媒体平台的兴起和其对传统网站的替代作用也被提及，尽管这带来了便利，但也导致了依赖中心化平台的问题。

44095250.article_content:
I recently decided to compile a
very large list of domain names
for the German country code top-level domain
.de
. I did this with the help of the
Common Crawl project
which provides a free, open repository of web crawl data and web graphs for the last years.
A few command line commands and a small
bash shell script
was all it took to compile a nice list of
roughly 9 million .de domain names.
💡
If you want to know more about how exactly I compiled the domain name list, just let me know and I might write about it in another blog post.
The resulting list is by no means complete and also not up-to-date, but it can be a nice starting point for further analysis and investigations. One of which I am going to write about in this post.
Enter the restaurant world
I was interested in domain names that belonged to restaurants and eating places in general. A simple but quite effective way to achieve this was to filter the domain names by German words that indicate such eating places:
Restaurant
Gasthaus
Gasthof
Gaststätte
Wirtshaus
Gastwirtschaft
Schänke
Speisewirtschaft
Speiselokal
Speisehaus
Speiserestaurant
Speisegaststätte
Gastlokal
Kneipe
Pizzaria
Since I was running this analysis on my windows desktop,
grep
was not directly available. So I used the
findstr PowerScript command
instead to do this filtering:
findstr /I "Restaurant Gasthaus Gasthof Gaststaette Wirtshaus ..." huge-domain-list.txt
This yielded a still impressive list of about
31.000 domain names related to German restaurants
.
Who's still alive?
Since I knew that the original list is outdated by definition, I had to check which domain names were still active. My first attempt to do this was also with a PowerShell script. This worked in principle and I was somewhat impressed by the capabilities that PowerShell provided, but at the same time the unfamiliar syntax turned me off and most importantly the speed was not great. So I created a small
Golang
program to get this job done, which worked great due Golang's
concurrency
features.
63% of the domain names were still active
(roughly 20.000 domains)
49% of the domains had redirects
(mostly from http:// to https://)
14% of the domains still serve http://
37% of the domains did not exist anymore
or returned other errors
Let's do some manual spot checks...
I was happy to have a list of
20.000 restaurant domain names
to work with and started some manual spot checks. After looking at 20 randomly selected websites from the list, I made two observations:
Domain Parking
was another group of domain names to filter out
Lieferando.de
had captured a significant number of domain names
I was not surprised about the first observation, because I had noticed already quite often that many good domain names are "parked". But
that lieferando.de thing caught my attention
. The domains that were captured by lieferando.de did not redirect to lieferando.de, but instead showed their logo and a link to their website.
How many of them?
With just a small extension to my
Golang
program I could find all the domain names form the initial list, that were captured by lieferando.de:
5.7% of the active domains from the restaurant domain list belong to lieferando.de
That is 1101 domain names. Here are some random examples:
elba-restaurant-knigstein-im-taunus.de
gasthauskaiser.de
grill-restaurantnaxos.de
henne-alt-berlinerwirtshaus.de
kulturkneipe-brotfabrik-bonn.de
The numbers are of course only estimates, since the initial domain list is not complete, but it provides some impression for the size of the topic.
When did it start?
I have not yet done a systematic analysis, but it seems (based on
WHOIS
entries for some domain names) that this "capturing" of restaurant domain names has started already before the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019 and continued at least until 2022 and potentially still continues.
(Preliminary) Conclusions
The number of "lost" domain names provides evidence that German restaurants have been struggling in the 2019-2023 time frame. It would be interesting to revisit this analysis in one or two years to see who many more domain names have become inactive or taken over by lieferando.
Lieferando is using aggressive tactics to drive traffic to their site. Maybe this can be described as
growth hacking
or a way of
SEO
. It is apparently not even new.
The extend to which lieferando is using this method suggest that it is at least somewhat effective and probably quite cheap to implement.
💡
What are your thoughts on this topic? When you sign-in, you can let me know in the comments.
44095250.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何利用Common Crawl项目的数据，通过简单的命令行和bash脚本，收集了约900万个德国“.de”域名。作者特别关注餐厅相关的域名，通过筛选与餐厅有关的德语词汇，最终得到约3.1万个餐厅域名。为验证这些域名的有效性，作者使用了PowerShell和Golang程序，发现其中63%仍活跃，49%存在重定向，14%仍使用http协议，37%已失效。进一步分析显示，其中5.7%的活跃域名被Lieferando.de捕获，显示了该平台通过捕获域名进行流量引导的激进策略。作者推测，这反映了2019-2023年间德国餐厅行业的困境，并暗示这种策略可能有效且成本低廉。
44095250.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：餐厅遭遇域名劫持和电话劫持的问题，在线平台的不道德商业行为，以及对当前互联网域名系统和在线存在的反思。

不同观点：
• TrackerFF 描述了一个餐厅老板遇到电话和网站劫持的问题。有人篡改了餐厅的电话和网站信息，导致客户无法联系到餐厅。当餐厅老板付费给某个公司后，电话和订单恢复正常，但停止付费后问题重现。这揭示了小型企业面对这种不道德商业行为时的困境。

• reustle 提到美国的外卖平台 GrubHub 也做过类似的事情，注册了大量域名并在谷歌地图上未经许可列出餐厅信息。这表明该问题不仅限于某个地区或公司，而是一个更为普遍的现象。

• ctxc 补充说，这些公司不仅创建假网站，还通过这些网站声称拥有谷歌地图的列表，然后勒索餐厅支付费用来修正信息。

• quaintdev 提出了一个更为广泛的讨论，认为当前的DNS系统和网站模型对普通用户过于复杂，很多人尤其是发展中国家的企业主更倾向于使用WhatsApp和社交媒体来进行在线营销。这揭示了传统互联网寻址系统的用户体验问题，并建议需要重新思考互联网的可发现性和身份问题。

• mousetree 批评 Lieferando 花费精力在注册域名上而不是改进应用，并指出其在柏林的糟糕服务体验。

• exiguus 建议将这种不道德行为曝光给媒体，以提高公众 awareness。

• ahmedfromtunis 提出小型餐厅可以通过先拥有域名来进行品牌重塑，尽管这并不是理想的解决方案。

• kleiba 指出这种行为可能已经违反了现有法律，但小型餐厅往往没有能力与大公司打官司。

• miohtama 提到越来越多的小型餐厅只做Facebook页面，避免复杂的网站管理，但这也导致了依赖中心化平台的问题。

• c16 调侃了Takeaway公司缺乏EEAT（专家经验、权威性、可信赖性），并建议谷歌应介入处理这种滥用行为。

• nubinetwork 怀疑 Doordash 也有类似行为，将讨论扩展到其他可能存在相同问题的公司。

• postepowanieadm 简单评论了德国法律系统的古怪，没有详细展开。

• weinzierl 提到亚马逊在早期也注册了大量域名，尽管数量上可能不如当代的域名抢注者。

• josefrichter 质疑域名在2025年的重要性，认为现在人们不再通过输入域名访问网站，因此域名的实际价值可能有限。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于餐厅老板面对的在线平台不道德行为，包括域名劫持和电话劫持，以及他们在面对这种行为时的无力感。
• 讨论中还涉及到对当前互联网寻址和在线存在系统的反思，有人认为DNS和传统网站模型对普通用户过于复杂，建议寻找更直观的方式。
• 社交媒体平台的兴起和其对传统网站的替代作用也被提及，尽管这带来了便利，但也导致了依赖中心化平台的问题。

data.title: Bagel: Open-source unified multimodal model
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源多模态模型的性能、应用及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• jjrv 分享了其在Ubuntu系统和RTX 3090 GPU上运行压缩版本模型的经验，指出该模型在硬件资源紧张的情况下勉强可以运行，但需要关闭其他窗口并降低屏幕分辨率。同时提到压缩版本与其原始版本结果应一致。
• spuz 对多模态模型中的“多模态”概念提出质疑，认为其通常只涉及文本和图像，而忽略了语音功能，并寻求能够结合语音功能的模型建议。
• akacrobat 对高质量开源多模态模型的稀缺表示认同，并询问社区是否有人对该模型进行过特定领域的微调实验。
• mdrzn 对模型的实际表现持怀疑态度，认为其在初步测试中未达到宣传效果，但仍希望其能实现所承诺的功能。
• charcircuit 对模型的性能提出批评，指出其在处理模糊问题时表现不佳，尤其在上下文理解和避免“幻觉”方面存在问题。

补充讨论：
• akoculu 提供了一个关于该模型的论文总结链接，供进一步了解。
• LourensT 对当前论文附带广告视频的现象进行了评论，暗示学术发布可能趋于商业化。
• GrantMoyer 强调该模型是Apache 2.0许可下的开源项目，指出了其开源性质。
• pleone 猜测该模型是否来自ByteDance团队，并询问社区对该团队的看法。
• mnky9800n 询问运行该模型所需的硬件配置，表明对硬件要求的关注。
• moffkalast 以幽默方式提到“The Everything Bagel”，可能意指模型功能的广泛性或复杂性。
• sandra_vu 询问该模型是否有商业化计划，表现出对模型未来发展的兴趣。
• wsintra2022 提供了一个相关新闻链接，可能包含更多讨论或背景信息。

争议焦点：
• 模型的实际性能与其宣传效果之间的差距是讨论中的一个争议点，mdrzn 和 charcircuit 均对此表示不满。
• 多模态模型是否应包括语音功能是另一个争议点，spuz 对此提出明确需求，但目前尚未有明确解决方案。

这些观点共同构成了对该多模态模型性能、应用及其技术细节的多角度讨论。

data.title: The truth about soft plastic recycling points at supermarkets
data.author: Kaibeezy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章揭示了英国超市软塑料回收计划的真相。调查追踪了40捆软塑料废物，发现其中70%被焚烧，而非回收，剩余部分则被降级回收为低价值产品，多数流向土耳其。环保组织ClientEarth警告，超市误导消费者。文章呼吁Sainsbury's和Tesco支持到2040年全球塑料生产减少40%，并推动减少一次性塑料包装，转向可重复使用系统。当前，全球正谈判制定《全球塑料条约》以应对塑料危害，文章鼓励公众签署请愿书以促进变革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软塑料回收及其替代处理方法（如焚烧）的有效性和可行性

不同观点：
• chimprich认为30%的软塑料被回收利用是一个不错的成果，并相信随着时间推移可以提高这一比例。他还认为，对已经分类好的塑料进行焚烧以回收能源是有效率的。
• stevep98指出一些特定产品，如Trex复合甲板，能够很好地利用回收的塑料，同时他也认为如果焚烧技术正确，焚烧并不是一个问题。
• PlunderBunny认为软塑料回收的结果取决于国家，如新西兰将软塑料回收制成围栏柱，并认为应进行研究而不是简单地否定或肯定回收。
• Scramblejams担心回收塑料中的有毒阻燃剂，认为在确保安全之前，埋葬塑料可能更安全。
• lotophage支持将塑料焚烧用于发电，因为塑料具有高能量含量，比褐煤更高效。
• meindnoch同样支持焚烧塑料，认为这样可以减少填埋，并减少对褐煤的开采。
• comrade1234指出在苏黎世只有PET塑料被回收，其他塑料都被焚烧发电，且二氧化碳被捕获再利用。
• Molitor5901认为应减少一次性塑料的使用，因为塑料难以回收，并提到自中国停止进口后，美国的塑料回收项目大多关闭。
• seanalltogether引用Penn和Teller的视频，认为只有玻璃和金属罐是真正的可回收产品。
• ninalanyon主张通过禁止塑料出口和非可再生塑料包装来加速塑料的减少和回收，并认为技术解决方案应由行业自行解决。
• Caelus9认为普通个人应尽量减少使用一次性塑料，但承认这在日常生活中具有挑战性。
• biofox认为将塑料转化为燃料颗粒也是一种回收形式，赋予其第二次生命。
• pfdietz建议将塑料分解回有用原料或单体，作为回收和焚烧之间的中间步骤，并认为应重点消除PVC等含氯塑料。

补充讨论：
• REDcycle在澳大利亚的失败案例（lotophage）显示出软塑料回收在实际操作中面临的困难。
• 关于焚烧技术的讨论，强调了现代焚烧设施的过滤和高效性（stevep98, comrade1234, worldsayshi）。
• 有关回收塑料的安全性问题，特别是与食品接触时的潜在风险（Scramblejams）。
• 强调政策和法规在推动塑料回收和减少使用中的作用（ninalanyon）。
• 不同地区对塑料回收和焚烧的处理方式不同，例如新西兰和苏黎世的案例（PlunderBunny, comrade1234）。

44095360.article_content:
Ever wondered what happens to the soft plastic that you return to the supermarket for recycling…?
…watch our film to find out
Share this video
Our new investigation reveals the
hard
truth about
soft
plastic recycling points at supermarkets…
🕵️ 40 bundles of soft plastic packaging waste were tracked through take-back schemes
across England over 12 months.
🔥 Of the tracked soft plastic packaging waste collected for recycling at Sainsbury's and Tesco stores,
70% of the soft plastic that reached a known destination was burnt, not recycled
🇹🇷 The rest ended up at recycling facilities that downcycle soft plastic waste into lower value products –
the majority of which were in Türkiye
.
⚠️ Environmental law NGO ClientEarth warns that the results of the investigation show that
supermarket soft plastic take-back schemes are misleading customers
.
🗣️ We’re now calling for Sainsbury's and Tesco to publicly support a
40% cut in global plastic production by 2040.
What happened to the soft plastic waste?
Collectively, these tracked bundles of soft plastic were found to have travelled over 25,000 km across the UK and overseas. Out of the trackers that we know reached a final destination…
What’s next?
The investigation shows that we urgently need to move away from false solutions.
We need to focus on eliminating unnecessary, non-essential single-use soft packaging and accelerating the transition to universally designed reuse and refill systems.
You can read our recommendations in full
.
Right now, world leaders are negotiating The Global Plastics Treaty – an international legal agreement to prevent the harmful impacts of plastic.
So we’re calling for the UK government to support a cut in global plastic production by 40% by 2040…
…and we want Sainsbury’s and Tesco to publicly support this.
✏️
You can help push for change. Add your voice now and sign our petition.
✏️
Already signed the petition? Click on the icons to share with your family, friends, colleagues, and community.
A bit of background
In 2021, supermarkets began to roll out an initiative to tackle the growing plastic problem – soft plastic packaging take-back schemes that claimed to help tackle the impact of plastic waste.
Supermarket communications around the schemes, along with revised on-pack recycling labelling, reassure customers that soft plastic is both recyclable and recycled – encouraging all of us to save up our salad bags, crisp packets, pasta packs, and pet food pouches at home, and drop it all off at supermarket collection points
.
Just over 10% of local councils collect soft plastic at the kerbside, and the waste industry widely acknowledges that there are significant challenges to recycling soft plastic.
"The truth is that finding a genuine solution for recycling soft plastic at scale is extremely difficult, if not impossible."
Sainsbury's and Tesco – between them – hold 43% market share of the UK supermarket sector. Both have widely rolled out soft plastic collection points to all their large stores. These take-back schemes encourage customers to collect their single-use soft plastic packaging at home and return it to the store, and are said to aim to increase recycling rates and reduce plastic waste.
Why is this important?
Plastic production is set to
triple by 2060
.
By 2050, global emissions from plastic production are estimated to account for
one-fifth of the Earth’s remaining carbon budget
.
Researchers warn that chemical pollution, also deriving from plastic use, threatens the stability of
global ecosystems and human health
.
Current estimates show that over
215 billion items
of soft plastic packaging are placed on the market each year in the UK
In 2022, only
7% of soft plastics
placed on the UK market were collected for recycling at the kerbside.
Want some more stats? Need a question answered? Then head to our Facts & FAQs page.
Read the full press release and contact us with any media enquiries.
Download images for social media and share the campaign with your network.
Please get in touch with any questions or thoughts about the campaign.
PRESS RELEASE
DIGITAL toolkit
get in touch
You can find a link to the report appendices
here
The Hard Truth About Soft Plastic
is an investigation by Everyday Plastic and
EIA
.

• comrade1234指出在苏黎世只有PET塑料被回收，其他塑料都被焚烧发电，且二氧化碳被捕获再利用。
• Molitor5901认为应减少一次性塑料的使用，因为塑料难以回收，并提到自中国停止进口后，美国的塑料回收项目大多关闭。
• seanalltogether引用Penn和Teller的视频，认为只有玻璃和金属罐是真正的可回收产品。
• ninalanyon主张通过禁止塑料出口和非可再生塑料包装来加速塑料的减少和回收，并认为技术解决方案应由行业自行解决。
• Caelus9认为普通个人应尽量减少使用一次性塑料，但承认这在日常生活中具有挑战性。
• biofox认为将塑料转化为燃料颗粒也是一种回收形式，赋予其第二次生命。
• pfdietz建议将塑料分解回有用原料或单体，作为回收和焚烧之间的中间步骤，并认为应重点消除PVC等含氯塑料。

补充讨论：
• REDcycle在澳大利亚的失败案例（lotophage）显示出软塑料回收在实际操作中面临的困难。
• 关于焚烧技术的讨论，强调了现代焚烧设施的过滤和高效性（stevep98, comrade1234, worldsayshi）。
• 有关回收塑料的安全性问题，特别是与食品接触时的潜在风险（Scramblejams）。
• 强调政策和法规在推动塑料回收和减少使用中的作用（ninalanyon）。
• 不同地区对塑料回收和焚烧的处理方式不同，例如新西兰和苏黎世的案例（PlunderBunny, comrade1234）。

data.title: How Does Claude 4 Think? – Sholto Douglas and Trenton Bricken
data.author: consumer451
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Dwarkesh Podcast的一集，由主持人Dwarkesh Patel与Anthropic公司的Sholto Douglas和Trenton Bricken讨论Claude 4的思维机制。他们探讨了近年来AI研究的进展，包括强化学习（RL）的扩展、模型思维过程的追踪以及实现全自主智能体的路径。Sholto专注于RL的扩展，而Trenton则研究机械可解释性。他们提到RL在语言模型中的成功应用，尤其是在竞争性编程和数学领域，但尚未展示长期的智能体表现。此外，他们还讨论了各国、工作者和学生应如何为AGI（通用人工智能）的到来做好准备。文章最后提供了与赞助商相关的信息和时间戳。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）的现状、能力、局限以及未来发展

不同观点：
• **fumeux_fume** 认为LLMs的主要问题在于缺乏专家反馈，这反映了模型只是基于模式匹配进行猜测，而非真正理解。他还批评将LLMs与获得普利策奖或诺贝尔奖联系起来的炒作行为，并质疑有关AI发现新药的传闻，认为这是 hype 没有实质证据。
• **vessenes** 则关注于LLMs在实际应用中的潜力，特别是其在取代白领工作方面的能力，并认为当前技术已经足够成熟，可以在许多领域取代人类工作，这是一个重要的转折点。
• **crypto420** 引用了关于强化学习（RL）在LLMs中的扩展可能带来不可预测结果的观点，并认为未来10-20年可能会出现非常不可预测的技术突破，甚至可能走向奇点（Singularity）。

补充讨论：
• **dcre** 强调通过这类访谈可以高效了解前沿技术的发展，并提供了之前类似访谈的链接以供参考。
• **arecurrence** 表示对访谈中讨论的当前技术挑战很感兴趣，并赞赏访谈中提供的论文链接，认为这有助于深入理解相关主题。
• **Der_Einzige** 关注于具体技术细节，质疑为何2019年发明的更好的采样方法（tail free sampling）至今未被广泛应用，并呼吁发明者给出解释。
• **cratermoon** 简短指出LLMs并不具备思考能力，这是一个直截了当的技术能力界定。
• **binary132** 只是简单提及了访谈的制作方，没有深入讨论内容。

争议焦点：
• LLMs是否只是基于模式匹配进行猜测，还是具备某种程度的理解能力（fumeux_fume vs. 其他观点）。
• 有关AI发现新药的传闻是否可信，是否是炒作。
• 强化学习在LLMs中的应用是否会导致不可预测且潜在危险的结果。

这些讨论反映了不同参与者对LLMs现状及其未来发展的多样化观点和关注点。

data.title: Giant Sequoias Are Taking Root in an Unexpected Place: Detroit
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 在底特律的Poletown East社区，树木学家正通过种植巨杉及其他树种来进行造林。该项目由Arboretum Detroit和Archangel Ancient Tree Archive两个非营利组织合作，始于2020年和2021年，种植了20棵巨杉，并在今年地球日种植了约100棵巨杉树苗。这些树苗是加州两棵著名巨杉的克隆体，包括Amos Alonzo Stagg树。尽管巨杉原产于加州，但在密歇根州表现良好。种植这些树木的目的是减少空气污染、降低温度、改善居民生活质量，并应对本地树种的生长困境。最终目标是将这个满是空地和废弃建筑的社区改造成未来的森林。树木学家还计划通过教育当地学童，培养他们成为城市森林的守护者。Archangel Ancient Tree Archive还计划在洛杉矶、奥克兰及伦敦种植巨杉，推动全球造林革命。

Arborists are reforesting Detroit's Poletown East neighborhood with giant sequoias and other species of trees.
AP Photo / Paul Sancya
Giant sequoias are typically found in California’s Sierra Nevada mountain range, where they reach heights of up to 300 feet.
Now, however, with help from conservationists, the world’s largest trees are spreading to new places. In Detroit, arborists are planting dozens of giant sequoia saplings in a blighted area in hopes of creating an urban forest that will clean the air, provide shade and, overall, improve residents’ quality of life.
The trees are being planted in Detroit’s Poletown East neighborhood through a partnership between two nonprofits, Arboretum Detroit and Archangel Ancient Tree Archive.
The effort started in 2020 and 2021, with the planting of 20 giant sequoia trees on private property and vacant lots owned by Arboretum Detroit. It continued late last month, as volunteers convened on Earth Day to plant roughly
100 additional saplings
.
“There’s not another urban area I know of that has the kind of potential that we do to reforest,” says Andrew “Birch” Kemp, co-director and board president of Arboretum Detroit, to the
Associated Press
’ Corey Williams. “We could all live in shady, fresh air beauty. It’s like no reason we can’t be the greenest city in the world.”
The Earth Day saplings are roughly a foot tall. But, if all goes as planned, they’ll rocket to roughly 15 feet tall—and counting—over the next decade. The trees can grow up to two feet each year.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Archangel Ancient Tree Archive (@archangelancienttree)
The saplings are all clones of two well-known trees in California. One is the Amos Alonzo Stagg tree, which measures 243 feet tall. Nicknamed “Stagg” for short, the tree is the
fifth-largest in the world
. The other, known as Waterfall, had the largest ground perimeter of any giant sequoia, 140 feet, before it was
killed
in a 2020 wildfire, reports
MLive.com
’s Justine Lofton.
The clones were developed by experts with Archangel Ancient Tree Archive, which traveled to California to gather the trees’ cones and new-growth clippings in 2010. The group is working to propagate and preserve the world’s old-growth trees at its headquarters in Northern Michigan, as well as in “living libraries” around the world.
Giant sequoias are not native to Michigan. And, yet, they’re somehow thriving in the state, which has a much cooler and wetter climate than their native California.
The biggest giant sequoia east of the Rockies is a 77-year-old specimen, called the
Michigan Champion
, that was planted in 1948 on the eastern shores of Lake Michigan. The tree measures roughly 116 feet tall and 5 feet in diameter.
“They’re safer here ... we don’t have wildfires like [California],” Kemp tells the Associated Press. “The soil stays pretty moist, even in the summer. They like to have that winter irrigation, so when the snow melts they can get a good drink.”
Meanwhile, experts say some native trees—including hemlock, elm and beech—are struggling in the city. In addition to the giant sequoias, Arboretum Detroit is also planting roughly 80 other species of trees in the neighborhood.
“We’re planting the forest of the future,” Kemp tells MLive.com. “Diversity is the answer. There are so many natives that aren’t happy here anymore. We have to look at what trees are thriving.”
The overarching goal is to reforest an area of Detroit that’s full of vacant lots, abandoned homes, an automobile assembly plant, a
former incinerator
and two interstates. The
University of Michigan
describes Poletown East as “arguably one of the most blighted neighborhoods in Detroit.”
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Arboretum Detroit (@arbdetroit)
Arborists expect the giant sequoias to reduce air pollution and lower the temperature in the neighborhood, which Kemp describes as a “heat island.” The trees will also sequester carbon dioxide.
Arboretum Detroit has also created a
network of parks
to help revitalize the area.
“We live in pretty much a pollution hotspot,” Kemp tells the Associated Press. “We’re trying to combat that. We’re trying to breathe clean air. We’re trying to create shade. We’re trying to soak up the stormwater, and I think sequoias—among all the trees we plant—may be the strongest, best candidates for that.”
Since giant sequoias can live for thousands of years, they’ll likely outlive the individuals who planted them. To help protect and care for them in the future, the groups are working with Detroit school children to encourage them to become stewards of the city’s urban forests. They call this educational effort “
propagating the propagators
.”
And Detroit is just the beginning. Archangel Ancient Tree Archive also wants to plant sequoias in Los Angeles and Oakland, California, as well as in London.

data.title: People who believe that AI might become conscious
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人工智能（AI）是否可能拥有意识的问题，以及当前科学界对此的研究进展。作者参与了一个名为"Dreamachine"的实验，该实验通过闪光刺激大脑，探索人类如何产生意识体验。研究人员希望通过了解人类意识的本质，进一步理解AI是否可能具备意识。尽管一些专家认为AI可能很快会拥有独立意识，但如萨塞克斯大学的Anil Seth教授等学者则持怀疑态度，认为这种观点过于乐观，且基于人类中心主义。文章指出，目前科学界对意识的本质仍无定论，但通过分解问题进行一系列研究，如"Dreamachine"项目，科学家们正努力解答这一重大科学和哲学问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）是否能具备意识，以及这种信念是否有科学依据。

不同观点：
• jqpabc123 认为，AI具备意识的观点类似于历史上的炼金术。他们指出，炼金术士在缺乏科学证据的情况下，坚信可以通过化学反应将铅变成金，这种"信仰"持续了几个世纪。jqpabc123 将这种现象类比为今天人们对AI的信仰，认为这种信仰更多是基于"信念"而非科学，并暗示这可能是宗教信仰的起源。

• OgsyedIE 则提出了一种支持AI可能具备意识的观点。他们引用哲学家丹尼特（Dennett）的观点，指出在现实世界中已经有无意识的事物（如精子和卵子）在特定条件下变成有意识的生命体（如婴儿）的例子。因此，他们认为AI具备意识的可能性也不应被完全排除。

补充讨论：
• jqpabc123 强调了对AI意识的信仰缺乏科学证据，并将这种信仰与宗教信仰进行类比，暗示这种信仰可能是不理性的。

• OgsyedIE 提供的例子（精子和卵子变成有意识的婴儿）试图说明从无意识状态转变为有意识状态在自然界中是可能的，从而为AI意识的可能性提供一种类比支持。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于AI意识的讨论是否应基于科学证据，还是可以依赖于类比和信念。jqpabc123 强调科学证据的重要性，而OgsyedIE 则试图通过自然界中的类比来支持AI意识的可能性。

• 另一个焦点在于类比推理的有效性。jqpabc123 可能认为类比推理（如炼金术的类比）不足以支持AI意识的观点，而OgsyedIE 则认为自然界中的例子可以为AI意识提供一定的支持。

The people who think AI might become conscious
9 hours ago
Share
Save

Science correspondent
•
@BBCPallab
Share

BBC
Listen to this article.
I step into the booth with some trepidation. I am about to be subjected to strobe lighting while music plays – as part of a research project trying to understand what makes us truly human.
It's an experience that brings to mind the test in the science fiction film Bladerunner, designed to distinguish humans from artificially created beings posing as humans.
Could I be a robot from the future and not know it? Would I pass the test?
The researchers assure me that this is not actually what this experiment is about. The device that they call the "
Dreamachine
" is designed to study how the human brain generates our conscious experiences of the world.
As the strobing begins, and even though my eyes are closed, I see swirling two-dimensional geometric patterns. It's like jumping into a kaleidoscope, with constantly shifting triangles, pentagons and octagons. The colours are vivid, intense and ever-changing: pinks, magentas and turquoise hues, glowing like neon lights.
The "Dreamachine" brings the brain's inner activity to the surface with flashing lights, aiming to explore how our thought processes work.
Pallab trying the 'Dreamachine', which aims to find out how we create our conscious experiences of the world
The images I'm seeing are unique to my own inner world and unique to myself, according to the researchers. They believe these patterns can shed light on consciousness itself.
They hear me whisper: "It's lovely, absolutely lovely. It's like flying through my own mind!"
The "Dreamachine", at Sussex University's
Centre for Consciousness Science
, is just one of many new research projects across the world investigating human consciousness: the part of our minds that enables us to be self-aware, to think and feel and make independent decisions about the world.
By learning the nature of consciousness, researchers hope to better understand what's happening within the silicon brains of artificial intelligence. Some believe that AI systems will soon become independently conscious, if they haven't already.
But what really is consciousness, and how close is AI to gaining it? And could the belief that AI might be conscious itself fundamentally change humans in the next few decades?
From science fiction to reality
The idea of machines with their own minds has long been explored in science fiction. Worries about AI stretch back nearly a hundred years to the film Metropolis, in which a robot impersonates a real woman.
A fear of machines becoming conscious and posing a threat to humans is explored in the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey, when the HAL 9000 computer attacks astronauts onboard its spaceship. And in the final Mission Impossible film, which has just been released, the world is threatened by a powerful rogue AI, described by one character as a "self-aware, self-learning, truth-eating digital parasite".
LMPC via Getty Images
Released in 1927, Fritz Lang's Metropolis foresaw the struggle between humans and technology
But quite recently, in the real world there has been a rapid tipping point in thinking on machine consciousness, where credible voices have become concerned that this is no longer the stuff of science fiction.
The sudden shift has been prompted by the success of so-called large language models (LLMs), which can be accessed through apps on our phones such as Gemini and Chat GPT. The ability of the latest generation of LLMs to have plausible, free-flowing conversations has surprised even their designers and some of the leading experts in the field.
There is a growing view among some thinkers that as AI becomes even more intelligent, the lights will suddenly turn on inside the machines and they will become conscious.
Others, such as Prof Anil Seth who leads the Sussex University team, disagree, describing the view as "blindly optimistic and driven by human exceptionalism".
"We associate consciousness with intelligence and language because they go together in humans. But just because they go together in us, it doesn't mean they go together in general, for example in animals."
So what actually is consciousness?
The short answer is that no-one knows. That's clear from the good-natured but robust arguments among Prof Seth's own team of young AI specialists, computing experts, neuroscientists and philosophers, who are trying to answer one of the biggest questions in science and philosophy.
While there are many differing views at the consciousness research centre, the scientists are unified in their method: to break this big problem down into lots of smaller ones in a series of research projects, which includes the Dreamachine.
Just as the search to find the "spark of life" that made inanimate objects come alive was abandoned in the 19th Century in favour of identifying how individual parts of living systems worked, the Sussex team is now adopting the same

data.title: Contacts let you see in the dark with your eyes closed
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于红外线接触镜技术的可行性、应用潜力和实际效果的讨论

不同观点：
• M95D认为，这种接触镜只能让用户感知到红外光的大致方向，但无法形成图像。用户不能通过这种技术“看到”红外图像或形状，仅能感知光的存在和方向。
• Caelus9提出，如果这种接触镜能在闭眼时帮助用户看得更好，它可能可以用于帮助盲人或视障人士，具有重要的社会应用价值。
• Baxtr引用了Xue的观点，指出该技术已经能让参与者通过红外接触镜准确检测到类似莫尔斯码的闪烁信号，并感知红外光的来源方向，但并不等同于“在黑暗中看见”东西。
• Bn-l对该技术的潜力表示认可，但指出当前技术只能检测来自LED光源的红外辐射，研究人员正在努力提高其对低强度红外光的敏感度。同时提到该技术在安全、救援、加密和防伪等领域的潜在应用。
• Harve9从文学角度提到，如果这项技术有效，它类似于Bob Shaw在《A Wreath of Stars》中描述的产品。
• Constantcrying强调，这种接触镜并不能让用户在黑暗中真正“看见”东西，它们只是在红外光照射时在可见光谱中发光，让用户感知到光的存在。

补充讨论：
• 该技术的实际应用效果存在争议，特别是它是否能够真正增强视力或帮助用户“看到”红外图像。
• 讨论中提到了技术的未来发展方向，如提高对低强度红外光的敏感度及其在多个领域的潜在应用。
• 部分评论者对该技术的社会影响和应用潜力表示乐观，尤其是其在医疗和安全领域的可能性。

data.title: MinIO Community version 2.0 is going back to be an object browser only
data.author: itherseed
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了MinIO的Object Browser（对象浏览器）项目。MinIO是一个开源的对象存储系统，而Object Browser是一个用于浏览和管理存储在MinIO中对象的工具。文章提到的内容包括项目的公开状态、通知设置（需要登录才能更改），以及项目的受欢迎程度（有336次分支和929个星标）。这表明该项目在开发者社区中具有较高的关注度和使用率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MinIO社区版用户界面功能的删除以及其对用户的影响

不同观点：
• itherseed认为，MinIO的更新日志中声称只是"弃用"某些功能，但实际上是从社区版的UI中去除了这些功能，并引导用户使用付费版本。他引用了具体的更新日志条目，并表达了对这种做法的不满，认为“Deprecated support”有误导之嫌。
• elashri提到，有人已经将最后一个包含这些功能的版本进行了分支，但对该项目未来的发展及其能否获得关注表示不确定。他还询问是否有其他类似的替代软件。
• jacksgt也在寻找自托管/本地部署的S3管理软件，并特别提到需要一个带有S3管理UI的解决方案，以替代MinIO。
• egorfine指出，实际上这些功能并没有被完全移除，只是从网页UI中去掉了，用户仍然可以通过`mc`命令行工具使用这些功能。

补充讨论：
• itherseed引用的PR（Pull Request）链接显示了删除UI功能的实际代码变更，并提到该PR的讨论已被锁定，暗示社区对这一变更存在争议。
• elashri提供了一个分支项目的链接（https://github.com/OpenMaxIO/openmaxio-object-browser），显示社区中有人尝试维护旧版功能。
• rhim提到在Reddit上有一个相关的讨论（https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/comments/1kva3pw/avoid_m...），暗示这个话题在其他社区中也在引发讨论。

争议焦点：
• MinIO社区版UI功能的删除是否合理，以及这种做法是否对用户有误导性。
• 社区对这种变更的反应，以及是否有可行的替代方案或分支项目。

data.title: Bitmap Images in 1965 – Mariner 4
data.author: oliverkwebb
data.article_summary: 1965年7月14日，水手4号探测器成功飞越火星，传回了首批火星图像。与月球或地球探测器通常采用的模拟图像传输不同，水手4号使用数字格式传输数据，以确保跨行星距离的清晰度。它拍摄了21张照片，每像素用6位数字表示，其中63代表黑色，0代表白色，与现代标准相反。图像以200x200像素的形式通过连续传输比特数据送回地球。最初，这些数据记录在磁带上，并通过扫描转印到胶片上进行修复。如今，利用现代工具可以将这些6位像素数据转换为RGB格式，并进一步转为PNG或JPG等常见图像格式，只需处理每3字节包含4像素的位操作。水手4号的图像处理展示了早期数字图像技术的雏形。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44091341.article_content:
On July 14th, 1965, the
Mariner 4
spacecraft flew by Mars, the first
to ever reach the planet successfully. In the scientific data it recorded, it took 21 pictures, similar space
probes built for the moon or earth would usually transmit image data back in a analog format of continuous
scan-lines (similar to a TV broadcast). But for clarity across interplanetary distances, This probe had
to record and transmit its data back in a digital format.
The clearest image from Mariner 4, with pixels visible
.bmp-1965
Image data from this was transmitted back as a series of bits, with a 6 bit number per pixel.
Weirdly enough, the highest number (63, 0b111111) represented black whilst 0 represented white,
the opposite of how its represented today.
The first image from Mariner 4, white parts showing gaps in transmission and highlighting pixel boundaries.
These pixels would be transmitted continuously to send a 200x200 image.
Digitializing this format
From here, these pixels would be recorded as dots on a tape, this tape would
be scanned to imprint the image onto film, and finer restoration work would
be done to perfect the picture. This is an example of an early dot-matrix
image printer.
Now, with modern computers and image formats, this data format does not
have to be imprinted onto tape to be viewed, converting this to raw
RGB data is fairly easy, and from there, you can convert that to
png/jpg/etc using tools like XPM or
farbfeld
(which is just 16-bit ARGB). The only hard part of this process is
that Mariner 4 image data works with 6 bit pixels, which means that
you have to work with chunks of 4 pixels (3 bytes) at a time.
Doing bit the manipulation needed to pack the image data efficiently,
any 200x200 image can be converted and viewed as if it came from the
antenna of a 1960’s space probe.
See Also
Appointment on the Moon
by Richard S. Lewis - Information in the chapter “No Hiding Place” was the inspiration for this article.

mar4-ff

data.author: DavidSJ
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dan Vanderkam解决Boggle问题及其技术细节和影响

不同观点：
• [smcin, danvk(原博主)] Dan Vanderkam自2004年以来独自研究Boggle问题，利用Google硬件进行大量计算，并在博客中记录了整个过程。他认为自己是唯一对这个问题感兴趣的人，并宣布成功解决了这个问题。
• [robinhouston] 对Financial Times报道这一故事感到意外，因为这类技术性内容通常先在Hacker News等技术社区传播，而不是主流媒体。他好奇FT记者是如何发现这个故事的。
• [sireat] 对Dan的成就表示赞赏，并提到在算法课程中可以使用Boggle问题作为Branch and Bound算法的示例。同时，提出需要了解在Boggle问题中计算上界和下界估计的具体方法。
• [cgreerrun] 对使用C++和Python组合的开发方式表示赞同，认为这种组合在原型速度和性能之间取得了良好平衡。
• [throwaway81523] 对计算资源和时间进行了比较，指出Google Cloud服务器与Ryzen 5950X等租用服务器之间的性能和成本差异。
• [jebarker] 对Dan的坚持精神表示钦佩，认为这种“低地位”问题同样值得关注，并将其与新发现的最大梅森素数相提并论。

data.title: Big banks explore venturing into crypto world together with joint stablecoin
data.author: wslh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：stablecoins的用途、优势、争议及其与传统银行系统的关系

不同观点：
• **支持stablecoins的观点**：
  - **可编程货币**：[scyclow] 指出stablecoins允许可编程货币，避免了传统加密货币价格波动的问题。例如，可以通过智能合约实现特定条件下的资金转移。
  - **效率提升**：部分评论认为stablecoins比传统银行系统更快、更有效，特别是在跨境交易和规避旧技术限制方面具有优势。

• **质疑stablecoins的观点**：
  - **银行参与的必要性**：[highfrequency] 质疑如果银行能够解决技术和监管问题，是否还有必要使用stablecoins作为USD的包装。
  - **合法性和监管问题**：[thunkle] 提出World Liberty Financial与特朗普家族及中东特使的资金关联，质疑其中潜在的利益冲突和合法性问题。
  - **潜在风险**：[Ekaros] 认为stablecoins可能被用于拒绝归还用户资金，这在传统货币系统中更难实现。

• **对stablecoins未来发展的看法**：
  - **竞争与整合**：[Mengkudulangsat] 认为stablecoins市场正在经历一场“逐底竞争”，从Tether到Circle再到传统银行，未来可能由美联储发行最权威的stablecoins。
  - **不可避免的银行参与**：[nailer] 认为银行最终会想要创建和持有自己的stablecoin，以在市场中占据一席之地。

• **对银行系统的信任**：
  - **对银行系统的批评**：[jbs789] 指出银行的缓慢部分是因为反洗钱(AML)和了解客户(KYC)的控制措施，而这些控制措施同样适用于stablecoins。
  - **银行创造货币的能力**：[_heimdall] 认为美国银行已经能够快速创造货币，因此stablecoins的必要性不明确。

补充讨论：
• **对整体金融环境的担忧**：[nickysielicki] 对财政部可能导致stablecoins系统崩溃表示担忧，质疑stablecoins相对于传统货币的稳定性。
• **与Ripple/XRP的比较**：[thatguyagain] 提到Ripple/XRP的初衷是为银行提供快速和安全的交易，质疑银行为什么不自己创建网络而是依赖第三方。
• **对评论质量的批评**：[monero-xmr] 批评Hacker News/YC在加密货币领域的讨论质量，认为很多并购活动未被正确理解。

争议的焦点：
• stablecoins是否真正提供了比传统银行系统更有效、更安全的解决方案，还是仅仅是现有系统的重复。
• stablecoins的合法性和潜在风险，特别是在利益冲突和资金安全方面的问题。

data.title: Violating memory safety with Haskell's value restriction
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了Haskell中由于多态引用可能导致的内存安全问题，并与ML风格语言的“值限制”进行对比。文章通过一个不安全的代码示例展示了在允许多态引用的情况下，如何破坏类型和内存安全。在Haskell中，由于`IO`类型的特殊性，多态类型无法被泛化，从而避免了类似问题。这是因为`IO`的泛型参数位于外部，使得绑定值始终是单态的。

文章进一步探讨了在其他单子（如`Identity`）中是否可以泛化`do`绑定。提出了一个类型类`MonadGen`，用于定义可以安全泛化绑定的单子。总体而言，Haskell通过其类型系统和单子结构，避免了多态引用带来的安全隐患，类似于ML语言中的值限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Haskell中解包IO构造是否安全，以及与Rust中内存安全问题的比较。

不同观点：
• tomsmeding认为解包IO构造函数是不安全且不正常的，因为这可能会导致内存安全问题，并可用于构建自己的unsafePerformIO。他对此感到惊讶，并质疑是否有人认为这是正常且安全的。
• jwatzman将Haskell的情况与Rust进行比较，指出在Rust中，任何不使用`unsafe`的代码遇到内存错误都被视为bug。他询问Haskell是否有类似的明确界线，以及哪些操作（如调用`unsafePerformIO`或`unsafeCoerce`）被视为导致内存问题的bug。他还提出疑问，Haskell中解包IO是否属于“自担风险”的操作，或者是否应被视为语言中的bug。

补充讨论：
• internet_points对`State#`与`unsafe`操作的关联表示关注，并表示以后会注意这一点。
• nssnsjsjsjs认为这种关于IO行为的解释很酷，且在某种程度上是直观的，但自己可能无法详细解释原因。

争议焦点：
• 解包IO构造函数是否被视为正常且安全的操作，还是应被视为潜在的安全风险并避免使用。
• Haskell中是否存在类似Rust的明确安全指南，即哪些操作可能导致内存安全问题并应被视为bug。

总结：
讨论围绕Haskell中解包IO构造函数的安全性展开，涉及其潜在的内存安全风险及与Rust安全机制的比较。不同参与者对此操作的安全性及语言设计中的相关指引存在不同看法和理解。

Violating memory safety with Haskell's value restriction
17 May 2025
A common issue in impure ML-style languages with polymorphism and
mutable references is the possibility of
polymorphic
references
.
In a hypothetical impure language that had both these features, but
no mitigations against polymorphic references, the following code would
be extremely unsafe.
unsafeCoerce ::
a
->
b
unsafeCoerce x
=
let
dangerous
=
ref
Nothing
dangerous
:=
Just
x
case
dangerous
of
Nothing
->
error
"unreachable"
Just
y
->
y
This code creates a reference
dangerous
with an initial
value of
Nothing
, writes
x
to it, and then
reads from it again. But because this language doesn’t prevent
polymorphic references and
Nothing
has type
forall a. Maybe a
,
dangerous
is actually
generalized
to
forall a. Ref (Maybe a)
. This means
that in the line that writes to it,
dangerous
is
instantiated to
Maybe a
, whereas in the line that
reads
from it, it is instantiated to
Maybe b
,
although the value stored in it still has type
a
, breaking
type safety and consequently memory safety!
Scary, right?
You might think that you could prevent this by just preventing
generalization of reference types, but references can be hidden behind
closures, so languages need a slightly blunter hammer: the
value
restriction
.
The value restriction says that a let binding can only ever be given
a polymorphic type if its bound expression is syntactically a “value”,
i.e. an expression that obviously will not perform any computation.
5
is a value. So is
Nothing
. But
sqrt 42
and (crucially)
ref Nothing
are
not
values and will not be generalized.
1
Haskell’s
let bindings do not have a value restriction.
So, does this mean that Haskell’s type system is deeply unsound and
we just never noticed?
No! If we translate the original example to Haskell, we will hit a
type error, telling us that
dangerous
was
not
generalized.
unsafeCoerce ::
a
->
b
unsafeCoerce x
=
do
dangerous
<-
newIORef
Nothing
writeIORef dangerous (
Just
x)
result
<-
readIORef dangerous
case
result
of
Nothing
->
error
"unreachable"
Just
y
->
y
MonadGen.hs:82:19:
error
: [
GHC-25897
]
• Couldn't match type ‘a’ with ‘b’
Expected: IO b
Actual: IO a
But the interesting question here is:
Why
was it not
generalized? To answer that, we will have to take a small step back.
What even is an IO
The important detail in this Haskell code is that
dangerous
was
not
bound in a
let
binding. It was bound in a monadic
do
-binding.
IO
is famously a monad, so a
do
-binding
like this is just syntactic sugar for an application of
(>>=)
, which (specialized to
IO
) has the
following type.
(>>=) ::
forall
a b
.
IO
a
->
(a
->
IO
b)
->
IO
b
So the value passed to the continuation (corresponding to the
variable in the let binding) has whatever type is wrapped
inside
the
IO
type constructor of its first
argument.
Now,
newIORef Nothing
can itself have a polymorphic
type.
newIORef
Nothing
::
forall
a
.
IO
(
IORef
(
Maybe
a))
However, notice that the polymorphic forall quantifier occurs
outside
the
IO
! This means that the value passed
to the continuation of
(newIORef Nothing >>=)
will
always have type
IORef _
and therefore be
monomorphic
. We can instantiate the
a
with
forall a. Maybe a
, but that only gives us a perfectly safe
IORef (forall a. Maybe a)
2
,
not
a
forall a. IORef (Maybe a)
.
That’s the magic! The placement of the
IO
in the types
prevents giving
dangerous
a polymorphic type.
What I really want you to appreciate here is just how similar this is
to the traditional value restriction. If we’re allowed to do arbitrary
effects, we might create a polymorphic reference, so ML bans all let
bindings that look like they might perform effects, whereas Haskell
already has a distinction between pure and effectful let bindings
(
>>=
) and just needs to prevent the second group from
being generalized.
Generalizable Monads
This hopefully all seems reasonable so far.
IO
can
create mutable references so we need to prevent it from generalizing
them and that’s why the monadic interface imposes something resembling
the value restriction.
But…
IO
is not the only monad. If we look at
Identity
,
it’s a monad that quite literally does nothing, so a
do
-binding in
Identity
is just a pure
let
-binding. Shouldn’t we at least be able to generalize
do
-bindings in a trivial monad like this?
Let’s think through what that would mean. Above, we couldn’t
generalize
newIORef Nothing
because it had type
forall a. IO (IORef (Maybe a))
with the
forall
on the
outside
. If it had type
IO (forall a. IORef (Maybe a))
, we could instantiate the
a
parameter to
(>>=)
with
forall a. IORef (Maybe a)
and therefore generalize it.
Coming back to
Identity
, we can generalize Identity
bindings, if for any context
f
(e.g.
f ~ IORef
), we can turn something of type
forall a. Identity (f a)
into something of type
Identity (forall a. f a)
. More generally, we can define a
type class for monads where we can generalize bindings this way.
class

44062576.article_summary:
文章讨论了Haskell中由于多态引用可能导致的内存安全问题，并与ML风格语言的“值限制”进行对比。文章通过一个不安全的代码示例展示了在允许多态引用的情况下，如何破坏类型和内存安全。在Haskell中，由于`IO`类型的特殊性，多态类型无法被泛化，从而避免了类似问题。这是因为`IO`的泛型参数位于外部，使得绑定值始终是单态的。

文章进一步探讨了在其他单子（如`Identity`）中是否可以泛化`do`绑定。提出了一个类型类`MonadGen`，用于定义可以安全泛化绑定的单子。总体而言，Haskell通过其类型系统和单子结构，避免了多态引用带来的安全隐患，类似于ML语言中的值限制。

data.title: GitHub issues is almost the best notebook in the world
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Simon Willison认为GitHub Issues几乎是最好的笔记工具。它免费且不限公共或私密笔记，全面支持Markdown，包括语法高亮，并可直接拖放图片或视频。它具有出色的链接能力，可以轻松引用其他仓库的Issues，并自动显示标题和反向链接。其强大的搜索功能可以在单个或所有仓库中查找笔记，甚至在整个GitHub中搜索。此外，它提供全面的API，支持笔记导出和创建，结合GitHub Actions还能实现自动化。唯一不足的是缺乏同步的离线支持，因此作者在手机上仍使用Apple Notes。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用GitHub issues进行项目管理和个人信息管理的利弊，以及对集中化和隐私问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• [支持使用GitHub issues] styfle分享了自己使用GitHub issues成功管理婚礼筹备和搬家打包的经历，强调其标签和搜索功能带来的便利。fbnlsr也表示认同，认为GitHub issues是他多年寻找的最佳笔记应用。bob1029进一步指出，在组织中使用issues可以有效集中管理项目，甚至让中层管理者脱离邮件的困扰。
• [对当前搜索功能的批评] eviks指出GitHub的搜索功能存在缺陷，尤其是在查找评论和处理拼写错误时不够智能。
• [隐私担忧] cogogo对使用GitHub存储私人笔记表示担忧，特别是对于微软是否会利用这些数据训练LLM（大语言模型）表示怀疑。bgwalter补充说，如果丢失2FA（双因素认证）可能会导致无法访问自己的计划，因此认为传统笔记本甚至纸笔更可靠。
• [去中心化和联合协作] Tepix强调去中心化的重要性，认为开发者社区应避免依赖像GitHub这样的集中化平台，并指出联合协作功能（如GitLab的合并请求）的缺失。他还提到政治因素可能影响对GitHub的访问，呼吁不要把所有资源放在一个篮子里。xeonmc也建议使用Codeberg或自托管Forgejo来避免供应商锁定。
• [工具对比] j_maffe和pier25将GitHub issues与Obsidian进行比较，暗示使用GitHub可能过于复杂。而_mikz提醒大家不要忘记GitHub issues的复选框和评论链接功能，认为这些功能有其独特价值。

补充讨论：
• [Apple Notes的离线功能] Jakob提到Apple Notes现在可以通过iCloud的“保持下载”选项实现离线使用，使得基于iCloud的应用具有类似Notes的离线同步功能。
• [移动端体验] pacifika提出了关于移动端使用GitHub issues的体验问题，暗示可能存在不便。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于GitHub的隐私问题和去中心化需求。一部分用户担心私人信息被用于训练AI或因政治因素导致访问受限，而另一部分用户则支持使用GitHub issues进行各种管理和笔记任务。

44094980.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
GitHub issues is
almost
the best notebook in the world.
Free and unlimited, for both public and private notes.
Comprehensive Markdown support, including syntax highlighting for almost any language. Plus you can drag and drop images or videos directly onto a note.
It has fantastic inter-linking abilities. You can paste in URLs to other issues (in any other repository on GitHub) in a markdown list
like this
:
- https://github.com/simonw/llm/issues/1078
- https://github.com/simonw/llm/issues/1080
Your issue will pull in the title of the other issue, plus that other issue will get back a link to yours - taking issue visibility rules into account.
It has excellent search, both within a repo, across all of your repos or even across the whole of GitHub if you've completely forgotten where you put something.
It has a comprehensive API, both for exporting notes and creating and editing new ones. Add GitHub Actions, triggered by issue events, and you can automate it to do almost anything.
The one missing feature? Synchronized offline support. I still mostly default to Apple Notes on my phone purely because it works with or without the internet and syncs up with my laptop later on.

data.title: Extending Minds with Generative AI
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了生成式人工智能（如ChatGPT）对人类认知和创造力的影响，指出人们对其可能带来的威胁和益处存在担忧。一方面，担心这些工具会导致作弊、削弱教育效果，甚至让人类失去创造和珍视自己内容的能力；另一方面，文章提出人类本质上是“扩展心智”，即利用外部工具增强思考能力，而非仅依赖生物大脑。作者认为，历史上新技术常引发类似担忧，例如柏拉图对阅读和写作的批评，但这些技术最终往往提升了人类能力。文章强调，尽管需要警惕技术的影响，但应避免将人类认知局限在生物大脑上，认识到我们天生具备利用外部工具的潜力。

Extending Minds with Generative AI
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Intelligence
Interdisciplinary studies
As human-AI collaborations become the norm, we should remind ourselves that it is our basic nature to build hybrid thinking systems – ones that fluidly incorporate non-biological resources. Recognizing this invites us to change the way we think about both the threats and promises of the coming age.
Sometimes, it seems like the world is full of techno-gloom. There is a fear that new technologies are making us stupid. GPS apps are shrinking our hippocampus (or in other ways eroding our unaided navigational abilities); easy online search is making us think we know (unaided) more than we do; multitasking with streaming media is driving down our native attention span and (possibly) affecting grey matter density in anterior cingulate cortex - see refs.
1
,
2
,
3
,
4
and for a balanced review
5
.
Similar fears surround new forms of generative AI (such as ChatGPT and others). These powerful tools – when properly prompted - can create novel versions of text, pictures, and other kinds of data, in ways that serve our needs. Will the ready availability of such tools encourage cheating and undermine educational practice
6
? Worse still, will it slowly rob us of both the need and the drive to create and value our own content? If we need to write a letter of complaint, plan a wedding, or compose an essay, perhaps we will simply fire up our favorite generative AI and uncritically accept whatever it offers? Wisdom suffers, collective self-plagiarism looms, and human creativity becomes all but obsolete.
When easy search, location services, constant access, and generative AI-based toolkits come together, they weave a complex web whose implications for humanity are far from clear. On the one hand, these webs empower us to do more and more, and more easily, than perhaps ever before. On the other, many fear they may rob us of more elusive goods. We might become content-curators rather than creators, and the passive targets of click-rate maximizing algorithms that do not have our best interests at heart. And what of human flourishing? Don’t these developments threaten to rob us not just of our time and attention but the very joy of creation too?
Grim portents indeed. But there are other ways to picture these emerging landscapes. There is ample reason to be alert and cautious – we’ll come back to all that shortly. But in thinking about the effects of all our new tools and technologies, we may often be starting from entirely the wrong place. The misguided starting point is an image of ourselves as (cognitively speaking) nothing but our own biological brains. An alternative vision, one that I have long championed, is that we humans are and always have been, what New York University philosopher David Chalmers and I call ‘extended minds’ – hybrid thinking systems defined (and constantly re-defined) across a rich mosaic of resources only some of which are housed in the biological brain
7
.
Yet we humans seem strangely resistant to recognizing our own hybrid nature. Instead, we have long harbored a highly restrictive image of ourselves – one that leads very naturally to the worry that new tools and technologies will lead to mental diminishment. In Plato’s
Phaedrus
, written around 370BC, we find a clear statement of the fear that new-fangled inventions such as reading and writing will have catastrophic effects on human memory. The fear was that these innovations would lead to lazy minds. We would start to think that we knew more than we really did, thanks to these cheap but superficial new means of non-biological storage and retrieval. Those fears seem laughable now. But we have not yet rid ourselves of their root cause – that deeply mistaken cognitive self-image. This is puzzling, especially since the history of our species is marked again and again by the transformative effects of newly discovered tools and practices. Arguably, it is our bedrock human nature to spread the load in this way – to become what I have called ‘natural-born cyborgs’
8
,
9
.
And yet, perhaps there was an element of truth even in the worries raised in the Phaedrus. Like most academics, I have often downloaded a paper and fooled myself into thinking I thereby – by some kind of electronic osmosis - knew what was in it. The advent of robust, reliably available, online search has added contemporary fuels to these familiar fires. Empirical studies have shown that the use of online search can lead people to judge that they know more ‘in the biological brain’ than they actually do, and can make people over-estimate how well they would perform under technologically unaided quiz conditions
2
,
10
,
11
,
12
.
But looked at another way (as the authors of these studies mostly acknowledge) these mistakes can also seem like quite a small price to pay
5
,
10
,
11
. As our tools and technologies have progressed, we have been able to probe ever further and deeper into th

data.title: Ask HN: Anyone struggling to get value out of coding LLMs?
data.author: bjackman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）在编程中的实际应用效果和价值评估

不同观点：
• y42和gyomu认为，LLMs在处理小任务（如代码补全、故障排除和解释）时非常有效，但在处理更复杂的任务时容易出现问题，导致使用者感到沮丧。他们强调，LLMs并没有达到取代人类工作的程度。
• bjourne则指出，自己仍然会亲自编写高质量的代码，AI只是提供建议和想法的工具，并未完全依赖。
• kragen引用“vibe coders”（氛围编程者）的概念，指出有些编程者对代码质量要求不高，依赖LLMs生成代码，但这种方式未必适合所有情况。他还质疑LLMs能否在所有领域显著提高生产力。
• avalys认为LLMs在学习和处理新库或API时非常有用，但在核心代码设计和架构决策上仍然依赖人工判断。
• elzbardico强调，LLMs在处理重复性、低复杂度任务时表现良好，但用户不应有过高期望，特别是在代码调试和设计方面。
• gwd指出，LLMs在处理跨多文件的复杂修改时效果不佳，但在某些情况下仍可作为辅助工具，帮助发现潜在错误。
• rikroots分享了自己使用Google's Gemini和ChatGPT的经验，发现LLMs在处理特定任务时表现不一，但总体上减少了对AI的恐惧。
• ZaoLahma认为，LLMs的价值在于处理小任务和节省时间，而不是生成完整的解决方案。
• lordkrandel指出，LLMs适合处理一次性代码，但不适合需要长期维护的项目，因为生成的代码难以维护和诊断。
• tootyskooty更倾向于手动管理上下文，以提高问题解决的效率，并通过分解任务来避免LLMs的错误输出。
• therealmarv提供了关于如何选择高质量模型和工具的详细建议，强调工具组合和提示优化的重要性。
• idw引用了Simon Willison的建议，为如何有效使用LLMs编写代码提供了参考。
• Sai_Praneeth表示，自己更喜欢直接将头脑中的想法转化为代码，而不是通过LLMs进行转换，认为使用LLMs沟通成本过高。
• pornell发现LLMs在处理小项目（100行以内）时表现良好，但在项目变得复杂（超过1000行）时容易出现混淆和错误。

补充讨论：
• LLMs在小任务和重复性任务上的有效性得到广泛认可，但在复杂任务和代码设计上的局限性也被多次提及。
• 不同用户对LLMs的期望和使用方式存在显著差异，一些用户将其视为提高生产力的工具，而另一些用户则对其持怀疑态度。
• 争议的焦点在于LLMs能否在所有场景下显著提高生产力，以及是否需要对生成的代码进行大量人工检查和修改。
• 工具选择和提示优化在提高LLMs效果方面的重要性也被多次强调。

• gwd指出，LLMs在处理跨多文件的复杂修改时效果不佳，但在某些情况下仍可作为辅助工具，帮助发现潜在错误。
• rikroots分享了自己使用Google's Gemini和ChatGPT的经验，发现LLMs在处理特定任务时表现不一，但总体上减少了对AI的恐惧。
• ZaoLahma认为，LLMs的价值在于处理小任务和节省时间，而不是生成完整的解决方案。
• lordkrandel指出，LLMs适合处理一次性代码，但不适合需要长期维护的项目，因为生成的代码难以维护和诊断。
• tootyskooty更倾向于手动管理上下文，以提高问题解决的效率，并通过分解任务来避免LLMs的错误输出。
• therealmarv提供了关于如何选择高质量模型和工具的详细建议，强调工具组合和提示优化的重要性。
• idw引用了Simon Willison的建议，为如何有效使用LLMs编写代码提供了参考。
• Sai_Praneeth表示，自己更喜欢直接将头脑中的想法转化为代码，而不是通过LLMs进行转换，认为使用LLMs沟通成本过高。
• pornell发现LLMs在处理小项目（100行以内）时表现良好，但在项目变得复杂（超过1000行）时容易出现混淆和错误。

补充讨论：
• LLMs在小任务和重复性任务上的有效性得到广泛认可，但在复杂任务和代码设计上的局限性也被多次提及。
• 不同用户对LLMs的期望和使用方式存在显著差异，一些用户将其视为提高生产力的工具，而另一些用户则对其持怀疑态度。
• 争议的焦点在于LLMs能否在所有场景下显著提高生产力，以及是否需要对生成的代码进行大量人工检查和修改。
• 工具选择和提示优化在提高LLMs效果方面的重要性也被多次强调。

• [r721] 并没有直接讨论材料的新颖性或物理特性，而是引用了之前的一个讨论链接（包含38条评论），暗示该话题之前已经被深入探讨过，可能没有太多新的信息或进展。

data.article_summary: The New Stack邀请软件工程领袖和有抱负的开发者加入其社区，通过新闻和独家内容帮助了解大规模软件开发动态。如果之前退订过，需重新订阅。The New Stack不会出售或与第三方分享用户信息。订阅需填写个人信息，包括姓名、公司、国家等，并回答一些问题以获取更相关的内容，如职位级别、角色、公司规模和类型等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言的演变、企业技术的持久力以及新兴技术对传统编程的影响。

不同观点：
• [anonzzzies] 认为尽管Java曾经为他带来了经济利益，但现在觉得PHP以及像SBCL这样的语言更有趣且速度更快。他对于为了金钱选择Java而非个人兴趣（如Lisp和Prolog）表示后悔，反映出对技术选择与个人兴趣之间的权衡。

• [tonyhart7] 指出，随着Go、Rust等新兴语言的崛起，Java等老牌语言可能会在未来20-50年内成为"遗留技术"。他还提到COBOL系统依然在某些企业中运行，暗示即使技术老旧，企业可能因历史遗留原因继续使用这些系统。

• [pjmlp] 表示在他的技术圈中，Java和.NET是主流，C++用于本地集成，TypeScript用于Web开发，而对于Hacker News上的流行趋势则不太关注，表明不同技术社区对技术选择的偏好和隔离。

• [omer9] 简单强调COBOL的持久影响力，暗示老旧技术在某些领域仍然具有重要地位。

• [dzonga] 认为社交媒体上的技术潮流（如LLMs、Next.js、tRPC等）往往夸大了实际影响，指出Java在企业后端系统中的不可替代性，特别是在大规模运行中的优势。他还提到LLMs在处理Java中复杂的模式（如AbstractFactoryBuilderClass、inverted inventor principles）方面并不显著。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Java等传统语言在未来技术领域的地位，以及新兴语言和技术（如Go、Rust、LLMs）对传统编程的影响和替代性。

• 不同技术社区对编程语言和技术趋势的看法存在差异，有的紧跟潮流，有的则坚持使用成熟稳定的技术栈。

• 企业技术选择的持久性与历史遗留问题也是讨论的重要方面，COBOL作为一个例子，显示了老旧技术在现代企业中的顽强生命力。

data.title: Ruffle – open-source Flash player
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: Ruffle 是一个开源的 Flash 播放器模拟器，旨在现代操作系统和浏览器上原生运行，安全地重现 Flash 内容。利用 Rust 和 WASM 技术，它避免了 Flash 原有的安全问题。无论用户还是网站所有者，安装都非常简便。Ruffle 采用 MIT/Apache 2.0 许可，免费开放使用，致力于将 Flash 重新带回网络。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：互联网档案馆如何处理Flash动画相关的网站展示

不同观点：
• klez认为互联网档案馆在展示基于Flash的网站时，自动应用了某种方式使这些网站正常显示。他提到自己访问了一个本以为无法工作的Flash网站，但通过互联网档案馆的Wayback Machine，该网站却运行良好，并且在加载时看到了那些熟悉的抽奖动画标志。这表明档案馆可能在背后做了自动转换或兼容处理。

• 另一层暗示的观点是，互联网档案馆可能采取了技术手段，使得原本因Flash停用而无法访问的网站能够继续展示其内容。klez对这种处理方式表示了一定的惊讶和认可。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点可能在于，这种方式是否真正保留了原始网站的体验，或者只是通过某种自动转换技术模拟了Flash效果。klez提到看到“raffle logos for a second while it loaded”，暗示转换可能并不完美或者存在延迟。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，klez对技术的实现表现出一定的兴趣或惊讶，表明他可能之前没有预料到互联网档案馆会采取这种方法来保留Flash内容。

• 最后，讨论还涉及了互联网档案馆的技术能力，以及其在保存历史网页和应对技术变革方面的努力和成就。这可能引发对其他过时技术的保存方式的进一步讨论。

44093204.article_content:
An open source Flash Player emulator
Made to run natively on all modern operating systems and browsers, Ruffle brings Flash content back to life with no extra fuss.
Safe to use
- Using the guarantees of Rust and WASM, we avoid the security pitfalls Flash was known for.
Easy to install
- Whether you're a user or a website owner, we've made it as easy as possible to get up and running.
Free and open source
- Licensed MIT/Apache 2.0, you're free to use Ruffle how you please!
Putting Flash back on the web

主要讨论点：AI生成内容的质量和其对人类创造力的影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：AI生成内容质量高，可以替代人类创作。一些用户认为，当前的AI工具（如GPT-4）生成的内容在质量上已经接近甚至超过人类普通创作者，特别是在技术写作、数据分析和基础编程等方面。支持该观点的例子包括AI在处理大量数据、自动化报告生成等方面的效率和准确性。

• 观点二：AI生成内容缺乏创造力和个性。持这种观点的用户认为，尽管AI能够生成高质量的文本，但这些内容往往缺乏深度、情感和个性。他们强调，人类的创造力、经验和情感是AI无法复制的。例如，一位用户提到AI生成的诗歌或小说缺乏真正的艺术价值和灵魂。

• 观点三：AI是辅助工具，而非替代品。部分用户认为，AI不应该被视为替代人类创造力的工具，而是一个强大的辅助工具。他们指出，AI可以帮助人类创作者提高效率，提供灵感和建议，但最终的创作过程和决策应由人类完成。例如，AI可以辅助作家进行头脑风暴或提供语法建议，但不能替代作家的独特视角和叙事能力。

• 观点四：对AI生成内容的伦理和版权担忧。一些用户担心AI生成内容可能涉及侵犯版权和知识产权的问题，特别是当AI模型基于大量未经授权的数据进行训练时。他们还提到，AI生成内容可能被用于传播虚假信息或操纵公众舆论，从而带来伦理和法律挑战。

补充讨论：
• AI生成内容的应用场景和局限性。讨论中提到AI在教育、医疗和科研等领域的潜在应用，但也指出其在需要高度专业知识和人类判断的领域中的局限性。

• 对未来发展的预期。一些用户对AI生成内容的未来发展持乐观态度，认为随着技术的进步，AI将能够生成更具创造力和个性化的内容。而另一些用户则持谨慎态度，认为技术的发展应伴随着严格的监管和伦理考量。

争议焦点：
• AI生成内容是否能够真正替代人类创造力，特别是在艺术和文学等需要高度个性化和情感投入的领域。
• AI生成内容的伦理和版权问题，特别是在训练数据的使用和生成内容的归属方面。

data.title: Domain Modelers Will Win the AI Era
data.author: nullhabit
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在人工智能（AI）时代，具备深厚的领域知识并能清晰建模的人将占据优势。过去，好的系统设计想法常常因为“实现鸿沟”无法转化为实际代码，而AI工具正在缩小这一差距。如今，关键不再是能否编写代码，而是能否明确构建什么。低层次的编码逐渐 commoditized，而定义实体、关系、约束和流程的能力变得稀缺和重要。AI可以帮助快速生成原型和迭代，但前提是用户必须对领域有深刻理解，否则生成的代码可能脆弱或逻辑错乱。文章强调，未来属于那些能够清晰建模领域问题的专家，他们可以利用AI更高效地实现自己的想法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件工程中的应用及对专业知识的影响

不同观点：
• [0x445442]认为，可以通过让AI学习过去的建模语言（如UML），并结合现代AI工具（如Claude）与软件设计工具（如Rational Rose），实现软件工程的自动化。这种做法可能会迎合管理层希望将软件开发流程商品化的需求。
• [lerp-io]对此持质疑态度，认为这种做法隐含的假设是AI能够比具备领域专业知识的人类专家更好地完成编码工作，这一点尚未得到证实，且可能低估了专业知识在复杂软件开发中的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [0x445442]的观点带有一定的讽刺意味，暗示AI如果能够完全取代人类在软件工程中的角色，可能会导致过度依赖工具而忽视人类专家的价值。
• [lerp-io]提出的疑问聚焦于AI在实际编码能力上是否能超越具有领域专长的人类，这是当前技术发展中的一个争议点，涉及到AI的能力边界和人类专业知识的不可替代性。
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否能够在软件工程领域完全取代人类专家，尤其是在处理复杂和创新性任务时，AI是否具备足够的适应性和判断力。

44093637.article_content:
← Back to Posts
Domain Modelers Will Win the AI Era
May 2025
Just needs a little guidance. And a floor plan. And a sense of direction.
“I knew what I wanted. I just couldn’t make it real.”
You had a clear vision: how a system should work, what the flow should feel like. But unless you could code, or convince someone who could, your ideas stayed stuck in mockups or Notion docs. Translators (developers, PMs, designers) only ever got it about 50% right. You were trapped by what I call the “implementation gap.” That gap is closing fast.
AI tools let you go from high-level intention to working code. If you understand the domain deeply, you can now build directly. Not by learning every syntax quirk, but by expressing your model clearly. The bottleneck has flipped. It’s no longer “can you code?” It’s “do you know what should be built?” This shift is bigger than most people realize.
Low-level code is becoming a commodity. Understanding what code to write isn’t. What’s scarce now is the ability to define entities, relationships, constraints, flows. The stuff that actually matters. AI will happily scaffold garbage for you. Without a model, it’s confident nonsense. But with a crisp mental model, AI becomes a multiplier. You can generate working prototypes fast. You can iterate without waiting on engineers. You can test real logic, not just sketch ideas on a napkin.
Consider something as simple as seat reservations. Let users pick a seat. Sounds straightforward, right? But if you’ve actually built this, you know the edge cases. Temporary holds vs confirmed bookings. Time-based release and locking. VIP access windows, group holds, overbooking policies. You can prompt an LLM all day, but unless you understand the rules of the domain, you’ll end up with brittle code or misaligned logic. The AI doesn’t know that a “hold” expires after 10 minutes, or that VIP members get early access, or that you need to handle race conditions when two people try to book the same seat.
You don’t need to be an “AI founder” to benefit from AI. You just need clarity. On what matters, how it works, and where the edge cases lie. That’s why domain modelers will win this era. It’ll be doctors modeling better workflows. Teachers building custom tools for students. Logistics experts automating scheduling logic. AI puts domain experts in the driver’s seat. If you’ve done the thinking, you can now do the building.
This is actually a return to something we lost. In the early days of computing, the people who understood the problem were often the ones who built the solution. Then we created layers of abstraction and specialization. Now AI is collapsing those layers again. Prompting is easy. Modeling is hard. But modeling is what makes the difference between a demo and a product. Between something that works in the happy path and something that handles reality. Don’t just chase what’s possible. Define what’s true.
The age of “I have an idea, I just need a dev” is fading. If you know your domain, AI lets you go from zero to real. I used to know what I wanted but couldn’t make it real. Now I can. And so can you, if you do the hard part first.

data.title: Scaling the Let's Encrypt rate limits to prepare for a billion active TLS cert
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary:
Let’s Encrypt目前为超过5.5亿个网站提供TLS证书，每小时签发超过34万个证书。为了应对高需求并保持响应速度，其基础设施依赖于速率限制系统。最初的MariaDB速率限制系统在服务增长后出现瓶颈，如数据库服务器压力大、重置时间长。

为了解决这些问题，Let’s Encrypt开发了一个新的速率限制系统，使用Redis和虚拟调度算法。该系统能够处理超过10亿个活跃证书，并有效减少MariaDB的负载。最初的速率限制基于每周每个注册域名签发的证书数量，但随着需求增加，数据库扫描操作变得昂贵且效率低下。

2021年，通过将API读取请求路由到数据库副本，减轻了主数据库负担，但高峰期的延迟问题仍存在。2022年，通过修补重复证书限制，允许用户逐渐恢复请求，改善了用户体验。最终，Let’s Encrypt认识到需要对速率限制系统进行全面改革，以适应未来增长。

44095334.article_content:
Blog
Scaling Our Rate Limits to Prepare for a Billion Active Certificates
By Samantha Frank ·
January 30, 2025
Let’s Encrypt protects a vast portion of the Web by providing TLS certificates to over
550 million websites
—a figure that has grown by 42% in the last year alone. We currently issue over 340,000 certificates per hour. To manage this immense traffic and maintain responsiveness under high demand, our infrastructure relies on
rate limiting
. In 2015, we introduced our first rate limiting system, built on MariaDB. It evolved alongside our rapidly growing service but eventually revealed its limits: straining database servers, forcing long reset times on subscribers, and slowing down every request.
We needed a solution built for the future—one that could scale with demand, reduce the load on MariaDB, and adapt to real-world subscriber request patterns. The result was a new rate limiting system powered by Redis and a proven virtual scheduling algorithm from the mid-90s. Efficient and scalable, and capable of handling over a billion active certificates.
Rate Limiting a Free Service is Hard
In 2015, Let’s Encrypt was in early preview, and we faced a unique challenge. We were poised to become incredibly popular, offering certificates freely and without requiring contact information or email verification. Ensuring fair usage and preventing abuse without traditional safeguards demanded an atypical approach to rate limiting.
We decided to limit the number of certificates issued—per week—for each registered domain. Registered domains are a limited resource with real costs, making them a natural and effective basis for rate limiting—one that mirrors the structure of the Web itself. Specifically, this approach targets the effective Top-Level Domain (eTLD), as defined by the Public Suffix List (PSL), plus one additional
label
to the left. For example, in
new.blog.example.co.uk
, the eTLD is
.co.uk
, making
example.co.uk
the eTLD+1.
Counting Events Was Easy
For each successfully issued certificate, we logged an entry in a table that recorded the registered domain, the issuance date, and other relevant details. To enforce rate limits, the system scanned this table, counted the rows matching a given registered domain within a specific time window, and compared the total to a configured threshold. This simple design formed the basis for all future rate limits.
Counting a Lot of Events Got Expensive
By 2019, we had added six new rate limits to protect our infrastructure as demand for certificates surged. Enforcing these limits required frequent scans of database tables to count recent matching events. These operations, especially on our heavily-used authorizations table, caused significant overhead, with reads outpacing all other tables—often by an order of magnitude.
Rate limit calculations were performed early in request processing and often. Counting rows in MariaDB, particularly for accounts with rate limit overrides, was inherently expensive and quickly became a scaling bottleneck.
Adding new limits required careful trade-offs. Decisions about whether to reuse existing schema, optimize indexes, or design purpose-built tables helped balance performance, complexity, and long-term maintainability.
Buying Runway — Offloading Reads
In late 2021, we updated our control plane and
Boulder
—our in-house CA software—to route most API reads, including rate limit checks, to database replicas. This reduced the load on the primary database and improved its overall health. At the same time, however, latency of rate limit checks during peak hours continued to rise, highlighting the limitations of scaling reads alone.
Sliding Windows Got Frustrating
Subscribers were frequently hitting rate limits unexpectedly, leaving them unable to request certificates for days. This issue stemmed from our use of relatively large rate limiting windows—most spanning a week. Subscribers could deplete their entire limit in just a few moments by repeating the same request, and find themselves locked out for the remainder of the week. This approach was inflexible and disruptive, causing unnecessary frustration and delays.
In early 2022, we patched the Duplicate Certificate limit to address this rigidity. Using a naive token-bucket approach, we allowed users to “earn back” requests incrementally, cutting the wait time—once rate limited—to about 1.4 days. The patch worked by fetching recent issuance timestamps and calculating the time between them to grant requests based on the time waited. This change also allowed us to include a Retry-After timestamp in rate limited responses. While this improved the user experience for this one limit, we understood it to be a temporary fix for a system in need of a larger overhaul.
When a Problem Grows Large Enough, It Finds the Time for You
Setting aside time for a complete overhaul of our rate-limiting system wasn’t easy. Our development team, composed of just three permanent engineers, typically juggles several co

data.title: Dependency injection frameworks add confusion
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在Go语言的工业应用中，依赖注入（DI）技术的价值及其常见问题。DI本质上是一个简单的概念，即将值传递给构造函数而不是在内部创建。通过使用接口，可以在生产环境和单元测试中传递不同的实现，如真实数据库和伪数据库。然而，依赖注入框架（如Uber的dig）虽然简化了多个依赖的管理，但也引入了运行时错误和调试困难，因为反射驱动的魔法导致编译时无法捕获一些依赖问题，错误信息也不直观。文章建议DI作为技术是有用的，但应谨慎使用框架，以免增加复杂性和调试难度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dependency Injection（依赖注入，DI）的优缺点及其适用场景

不同观点：
• **支持DI的观点**：
  - **简化测试**：surgical_fire指出，DI的主要好处是使代码更易于测试，特别是在处理时间等外部依赖时，可以通过注入模拟对象（mock）来测试特定条件下的行为。
  - **管理复杂依赖**：danpalmer认为，DI在处理多个环境、多个实现以及大量依赖时非常必要，可以避免手动管理依赖的复杂性。
  - **代码组织和维护**：latchkey提到，DI框架（如Uber's FX）帮助他组织代码，使其更易于测试和管理，特别是在处理启动/关闭、服务和日志记录时。
  - **接口编程和生命周期管理**：SillyUsername强调，DI确保代码依赖于接口而不是具体实现，有助于避免团队成员随意更改实现，同时DI容器还能管理对象的生命周期。

• **反对或质疑DI的观点**：
  - **增加复杂性**：lemagedurage指出，DI破坏了代码导航，使确定变量具体实现变得困难。
  - **隐藏细节**：fifticon提到，DI可能导致开发者不了解代码的底层实现，产生“自动导航”问题，并且可能导致不必要的性能开销和错误。
  - **不必要的框架**：superdisk认为，动态变量（如Lisp中的动态变量）可以实现DI的效果，不需要专门的框架。
  - **DI的局限性**：DanielHB表示，虽然DI在大的单体应用中可能有用，但在微服务架构中，通过mock外部服务可以达到类似的效果，DI的必要性降低。

• **中立或具体场景下的观点**：
  - **编译时依赖管理**：Fire-Dragon-DoL认为，DI在编译或启动时是有用的，但在运行时不一定需要，可以通过编译时变量改变实现。
  - **DI作为设计模式**：jillesvangurp指出，DI是一种设计模式，目的是将粘合代码与业务逻辑分离，适用于多种语言，强调代码的易测试性和可维护性。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：DI的复杂性与必要性是主要争议点。支持者认为DI有助于管理复杂依赖和提高代码可测试性，反对者则认为DI增加了不必要的复杂性并可能隐藏底层实现细节。
• **具体实现的批评**：有些评论对Java和Spring框架的DI实现提出了批评（如rr808和therealdrag0），认为这些框架导致了不必要的复杂性和维护困难。
• **DI的适用场景**：讨论中多次提到DI在大型项目中的必要性，而在小型项目或微服务架构中，DI的必要性降低。

总体来看，评论中对DI的态度呈现两极分化，支持者强调其在大型项目中的重要性和优势，反对者则关注其带来的复杂性和潜在问题。

Table of Contents
When working with Go in an
industrial
context, I feel like dependency injection (DI) often
gets a bad rep because of
DI frameworks
. But DI as a technique is quite useful. It just
tends to get explained with too many OO jargons and triggers PTSD among those who came to Go
to escape GoF theology.
Dependency Injection is a 25-dollar term for a 5-cent concept.
— James Shore
DI basically means
passing values into a constructor instead of creating them inside it
.
That’s really it. Observe:
type
server
struct
{
db
DB
}
// NewServer constructs a server instance
func
NewServer
()
*
server
{
db
:=
DB
{}
// The dependency is created here
return
&
server
{
db
:
db
}
}
Here,
NewServer
creates its own
DB
. Instead, to inject the dependency, build
DB
elsewhere and pass it in as a constructor parameter:
func
NewServer
(
db
DB
)
*
server
{
return
&
server
{
db
:
db
}
}
Now the constructor no longer decides how a database is built; it simply
receives
one.
In Go, DI is often done using interfaces. You collate the behavior you care about in an
interface, and then provide different concrete implementations for different contexts. In
production, you pass a real implementation of
DB
. In unit tests, you pass a fake
implementation that behaves the same way from the caller’s perspective but avoids real
database calls.
Here’s how that looks:
// behaviour we care about
type
DB
interface
{
Get
(
id
string
)
(
string
,
error
)
Save
(
id
,
value
string
)
error
}
type
server
struct
{
db
DB
}
// NewServer accepts a concrete implementation of the DB interface in runtime
// and passes it to the server struct.
func
NewServer
(
db
DB
)
*
server
{
return
&
server
{
db
:
db
}
}
A real implementation of
DB
might look like this:
type
RealDB
struct
{
url
string
}
func
NewDB
(
url
string
)
*
RealDB
{
return
&
RealDB
{
url
:
url
}
}
func
(
r
*
RealDB
)
Get
(
id
string
)
(
string
,
error
)
{
// pretend we hit Postgres
return
"real value"
,
nil
}
func
(
r
*
RealDB
)
Save
(
id
,
value
string
)
error
{
return
nil
}
And a fake implementation for unit tests might be:
type
FakeDB
struct
{
data
map
[
string
]
string
}
func
NewFake
()
*
FakeDB
{
return
&
FakeDB
{
data
:
map
[
string
]
string
{}}
}
func
(
f
*
FakeDB
)
Get
(
id
string
)
(
string
,
error
)
{
return
f
.
data
[
id
],
nil
}
func
(
f
*
FakeDB
)
Save
(
id
,
value
string
)
error
{
f
.
data
[
id
]
=
value
;
return
nil
}
Use the fake in unit tests like so:
func
TestServerGet
(
t
*
testing
.
T
)
{
fake
:=
NewFake
()
_
=
fake
.
Save
(
"42"
,
"fake"
)
srv
:=
NewServer
(
fake
)
val
,
_
:=
srv
.
db
.
Get
(
"42"
)
if
val
!=
"fake"
{
t
.
Fatalf
(
"want fake, got %s"
,
val
)
}
}
The compiler guarantees both
RealDB
and
FakeDB
satisfy
DB
, and during tests, we can
swap out the implementations without much ceremony.
Why frameworks turn mild annoyance into actual pain
#
Once
NewServer
grows half a dozen dependencies, wiring them by hand can feel noisy. That’s
when a DI framework starts looking tempting.
With Uber’s
dig
, you register each constructor as a
provider
.
Provide
takes a
function, uses reflection to inspect its parameters and return type, and adds it as a node
in an internal dependency graph. Nothing is executed yet. Things only run when you call
.Invoke()
on the container.
But that reflection-driven magic is also where the pain starts. As your graph grows, it gets
harder to tell which constructor feeds which one. Some constructor takes one parameter, some
takes three. There’s no single place you can glance at to understand the wiring. It’s all
figured out inside the container at runtime.
Let the container figure it out!
— every DI framework ever
func
BuildContainer
()
*
dig
.
Container
{
c
:=
dig
.
New
()
// Each Provide call teaches dig about one node in the graph.
c
.
Provide
(
NewConfig
)
// produces *Config
c
.
Provide
(
NewDB
)
// wants *Config, produces *DB
c
.
Provide
(
NewRepo
)
// wants *DB, produces *Repo
c
.
Provide
(
NewFlagClient
)
// produces *FlagClient
c
.
Provide
(
NewService
)
// wants *Repo, *FlagClient, produces *Service
c
.
Provide
(
NewServer
)
// wants *Service, produces *server
return
c
}
func
main
()
{
// Invoke kicks off the whole graph. dig topologically sorts, calls each
// constructor, and finally hands *server to your callback.
if
err
:=
BuildContainer
().
Invoke
(
func
(
s
*
server
)
{
s
.
Run
()
});
err
!=
nil
{
panic
(
err
)
}
}

NewFlagClient
. The code still
compiles
. There’s no error until
runtime, when dig fails to construct
NewService
due to a missing dependency. And the error
message you get?
dig invoke failed: could not build arguments for function
main.main.func1 (prog.go:87)
: failed to build *main.Server
: could not build arguments for function main.NewServer (prog.go:65)
: failed to build *main.Service: missing dependencies for function
main.NewService (prog.go:55)
: missing type: *main.FlagClient
That’s five stack frames deep, far from where the problem started. Now you’re digging
through dig’s internals to reconstr

• nikcub将Builder.ai与Theranos或WeWork类比，指出其类似于投资泡沫的兴起和崩溃，并提到多个关键事件，如CEO辞职、收入重述和公司倒闭。他预测在AI投资热潮中会有更多类似案例出现。
• empiko认为，许多AI初创公司将很快耗尽资金，指出一些公司虽然筹集了大量资金，但没有实际产品，正走向终结。
• krona提供了关于会计公司PKF Littlejohn合伙人之前与Builder.ai创始人有联系的信息，进一步揭示了公司治理问题。
• justinbaker84对VC频繁投资于欺诈性公司感到失望，认为这与投资于合法但不成功的公司不同，指出欺诈性公司更容易获得投资。
• spamizbad指出，即使是财务责任良好的AI公司也比典型的SaaS初创公司更资本密集，运营更具挑战性。
• gchamonlive认为，许多华而不实的AI应用无法在消费级硬件上运行，只是为了推动高成本的GPU使用，而非真正的实用应用。
• chuckadams讽刺地指出，如果Builder.ai更年轻，或许可以通过实际使用AI取得成功，但其前瞻性被用于欺诈，仍然是 fraud。
• greatgib提到公司试图通过现有股东筹集7500万美元来修复资产负债表，质疑投资者的决策。
• benbojangles描述了英国公司通过虚假成功、最大化贷款和债务然后倒闭或欺诈性股票发行而消失的现象，对商业环境感到失望。
• zpeti对Builder.ai在无人注意的情况下花费5亿美元感到困惑，质疑投资者为何如此愚蠢。
• bartread批评公司创始人的“首席巫师”头衔，认为这种不严肃的职位名称反映了不良商业决策，质疑投资者为何给予公司大量资金。
• conradfr简单评论了创始人头衔的硅谷风格。
• kwillets将英国科技界比作没有Sarbanes-Oxley法案的环境。
• nssnsjsjsjs提出了是否需要法律来保持工资在通知期内的意见。

补充讨论：
• Builder.ai的倒闭引发了对AI投资热潮中潜在欺诈和不良投资决策的广泛讨论。
• 讨论涉及公司治理问题，如创始人之前的关系和不当职位名称。
• 对英国商业环境的批评，认为存在系统性欺诈和不透明操作。
• 强调了AI公司的高资本需求和运营挑战，以及对实际可运行应用的需求。
• 投资者在追求高回报时对不良公司的容忍度和识别能力受到质疑。

data.title: Show HN: Rotary Phone Dial Linux Kernel Driver
data.author: sephalon
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个Linux内核驱动程序，能够将旋转拨号电话转换为evdev输入设备。通过该驱动，用户可以将老式的旋转拨号电话接入现代计算机系统，作为输入设备使用。项目遵循GNU通用公共许可证v2.0或更高版本，并于2025年1月1日创建。项目的详细信息和使用说明可参阅其README文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕rotary phone（旋转拨号电话）及其现代应用的技术讨论和怀旧分享

不同观点：
• **支持并展示rotary phone的现代应用**：
  - [anonymousiam] 分享了在70年代末通过HP41C计算器和旋转拨号电话实现自动拨号的项目，强调了通过技术创新将旧设备与现代技术结合的可能性。
  - [jtwaleson] 将rotary phone改装成蓝牙耳机，展示了如何将旧设备重新用作现代通信工具。
  
• **对rotary phone复古风的怀旧和技术设想**：
  - [mauvehaus] 提到曾建议将iPhone设计成带有iPod触控轮的形式，以复古旋转拨号风格，但被拒绝。
  - [Stratoscope] 通过分享30年前的经历，间接表达了对rotary phone时代的怀念。
  
• **技术实现及挑战**：
  - [jeroenhd] 讨论了用Rust重写驱动程序的可能性和遇到的困难，强调了文档记录技术探索过程的重要性。
  - [kevvok] 提到了Sarah通过编写驱动程序，使现代Linux系统与旧电话网络设备兼容的案例。
  
• **地域差异和技术变种**：
  - [bacon_waffle] 指出新西兰rotary phone的脉冲映射方式与常规不同，强调了技术标准的地域差异。
  
• **对现代需求的延伸**：
  - [reaperducer] 提到需要DTMF（双音多频）版本的旋转拨号转换器，分享了因现代建筑缺乏传统电话线路而无法继续使用rotary phone的遗憾。
  - [rcakebread] 提到通过Hayes兼容调制解调器使用旋转拨号，展示了rotary phone在现代通信中的一种应用延伸。

补充讨论：
• **对现代技术需求的不同关注点**：
  - [CodeBeater] 提到正在拆解和修理rotary phone，展示了对旧设备技术细节的兴趣。
  - [tempodox] 更关注现代Linux系统中蓝牙音频和UTF-8支持的问题，暗示了对旧设备复古应用兴趣不大，更在意现代技术的完善。

争议焦点：
• 主要体现在对rotary phone复古应用的热情与现代技术需求之间的不同优先级和兴趣点。一些人热衷于将旧设备改造为现代可用工具，而另一些人则更关注现代技术的功能完善和可用性。

data.title: The double standard of webhook security and API security
data.author: mfbx9da4
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：webhook和API请求的安全性、认证机制及其实现方式

不同观点：
• erikerikson：认为webhook调用通过签名验证来源，并且依赖于安全连接和证书验证。将认证转移到webhook实现者会导致需要处理多种认证系统，增加复杂性。
• maxwellg：倾向于使用HMAC，但承认API密钥对用户更简单，特别是在命令行使用和维护客户端库时。工具的进步也使得日志配置更加安全。
• btown：建议不要完全信任webhook，应采用异步重处理和设置标志的方式，以应对顺序错乱和重复请求等问题，从而降低签名验证的重要性。
• paradox460：对缺乏授权机制的webhook感到不满，认为像Stripe和Twilio那样使用签名验证是更好的做法，甚至可以接受HTTP基本认证。
• eqvinox：批评文章未深入考虑安全需求，认为API密钥机制不适合webhook，因为webhook是“API访问你”而不是你请求事件。建议使用额外的加密层来增强安全性。
• arkh、Retr0id：关注实现细节，如防止定时攻击，确保验证函数的 cryptographically sound。
• skybrian：解释了webhook中公钥分发的问题，认为API密钥在客户与供应商的单对多通信中更合适。
• slt2021：建议使用mTLS（或带有客户端证书的TLS）来验证调用者。
• arccy：认为请求签名在安全性上更好，但开发人员往往不愿意实现复杂的安全措施。
• kaoD：对TLS客户端证书不为人知和被忽视感到遗憾。
• h1fra：指出webhook需要验证来源和真实性，而API密钥用于验证请求者身份。
• michaelt：提到使用签名请求的API通常提供现成的库，接收方可以根据需要选择是否验证签名。
• olehif：指出签名允许服务器为所有客户端使用一个证书，而API密钥需要为每个客户端提供唯一密钥，签名更方便。
• felipemesquita：认为API请求已经过认证，签名带来的额外安全性有限，而webhook由于可能被未经认证的来源发送，因此需要签名验证。

补充讨论：
• 关于HMAC和API密钥的易用性和安全性讨论。
• 关于使用TLS和mTLS的优缺点。
• 关于防止定时攻击和确保加密实现安全性的技术细节。
• 关于公钥分发和认证机制在不同场景中的适用性。
• 关于签名验证在webhook中的必要性和实现方式的争议。
• 关于API请求和webhook请求在认证和安全性上的差异和处理方式的不同观点。

data.title: Demoting i686-PC-windows-gnu to Tier 2
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Rust 1.88.0将把i686-pc-windows-gnu目标从Tier 1降级为Tier 2。降级后，该目标的标准库和编译器构建仍将分发，但测试和支持力度会减少。目前，GNU工具链主要用于跨平台编译和避免MSVC的许可问题，但由于缺乏维护者及使用率低，32位windows-gnu目标问题频发。若未来仍无改善，可能进一步降级。依赖该目标的用户若具备相关经验，欢迎成为维护者。详见RFC 3771。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust平台支持和跨平台编译工具的讨论，特别是对Windows 32位目标平台的支持减少及其影响。

不同观点：
• [malkia] 提到有跨平台工具如`clang-cl`和`lld`，可以在无需Wine的情况下针对"MSVC"链接Windows可执行文件，暗示这些工具可以减轻跨平台开发的困难。

• [kstrauser] 认为Rust开发团队不再为少数人使用的平台（如32位Windows）放慢开发进度是合理的，并提供了数据支持，指出x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu平台的下载量远远超过32位Windows平台，显示主流用户的需求。

• [flohofwoe] 质疑此举是否仅影响32位目标平台，并指出目前是否还有支持的32位Windows版本存疑，暗示对32位Windows支持的必要性可能已经降低。

• [mmastrac] 同意此决定，指出调试Windows平台上的 obscure bugs 令人沮丧，尤其在没有本地Windows设置的情况下，开发体验更差，分享了在Deno工作的经验。

• [dblohm7] 表达了对维护*windows-gnu目标的兴趣，但因时间限制无法参与，显示出社区中有愿意贡献但受限于时间的潜在维护者。

• [jmclnx] 关注此决定对OpenBSD和NetBSD的影响，提到OpenBSD可能因此放弃更多依赖Rust的i386软件包，并推测NetBSD也可能受到影响，但目前因Cross-Compiling的假设尚未成为问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Rust团队是否应继续支持32位Windows平台，一方认为应照顾主流用户需求，另一方则认为即便有少数用户依赖，也应尽力提供支持。
• 社区中存在愿意贡献的潜在维护者，但时间和精力是制约因素。

44097637.article_content:
May 26, 2025 · Noratrieb
on behalf of
Compiler Team
In Rust 1.88.0, the Tier 1 target
i686-pc-windows-gnu
will be demoted to Tier 2.
As a Tier 2 Target, builds will continue to be distributed for both the standard library and the compiler.
Background
Rust has supported Windows for a long time, with two different flavors of Windows targets: MSVC-based and GNU-based. MSVC-based targets (for example the most popular Windows target
x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
) use Microsoft’s native linker and libraries, while GNU-based targets (like
i686-pc-windows-gnu
) are built entirely from free software components like
gcc
,
ld
, and mingw-w64.
The major reason to use a GNU-based toolchain instead of the native MSVC-based one is cross-compilation and licensing.
link.exe
only runs on Windows (barring Wine hacks) and requires a license for commercial usage.
x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
and
i686-pc-windows-gnu
are currently both Tier 1 with host tools.
The
Target Tier Policy
contains more details on what this entails, but the most important part is that tests for these targets are being run on every merged PR.
This is the highest level of support we have, and is only used for the most high value targets (the most popular Linux, Windows, and Apple targets).
The
*-windows-gnu
targets currently do not have any dedicated target maintainers.
We do not have a lot of expertise for this toolchain, and issues often aren't fixed and cause problems in CI that we have a hard time to debug.
The 32-bit version of this target is especially problematic and has significantly less usage than
x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
, which is why
i686-pc-windows-gnu
is being demoted to Tier 2.
What changes?
After Rust 1.88.0,
i686-pc-windows-gnu
will now be Tier 2 with host tools.
For users, nothing will change immediately. Builds of both the standard library and the compiler will still be distributed by the Rust Project for use via
rustup
or alternative installation methods.
This does mean that this target will likely accumulate bugs faster in the future because of the reduced testing.
Future
If no maintainers are found and the
*-windows-gnu
targets continue causing problems, they may be demoted further.
No concrete plans about this have been made yet.
If you rely on the
*-windows-gnu
targets and have expertise in this area, we would be very happy to have you as a target maintainer. You can check the
Target Tier Policy
for what exactly that would entail.
For more details on the motivation of the demotion, see
RFC 3771
which proposed this change.
44097637.article_summary: Rust 1.88.0将把i686-pc-windows-gnu目标从Tier 1降级为Tier 2。降级后，该目标的标准库和编译器构建仍将分发，但测试和支持力度会减少。目前，GNU工具链主要用于跨平台编译和避免MSVC的许可问题，但由于缺乏维护者及使用率低，32位windows-gnu目标问题频发。若未来仍无改善，可能进一步降级。依赖该目标的用户若具备相关经验，欢迎成为维护者。详见RFC 3771。
